Sports.title: Pioneer behind Sunderland’s Stadium of Light in ‘fantasy land’ after booking Europa League trip to Milan
Sports.content:
SIR BOB MURRAY built the ground fit to stage European football.

The 80-year-old, however, admits he never envisioned his beloved Black Cats playing in Europe there.



Murray, the son of a Sunderland coal miner, began his love affair with the club “from birth” and it blossomed with every visit to Roker Park.

Like every boy, he grew up hoping to one day play there while watching on from the Fulwell End. Instead, he went on to OWN them.



Before replacing Tom Cowie as chairman in 1986, the lifelong fan had watched his team win the 1973 FA Cup but missed out on the resulting European campaign.

Attempting to cash in on the excitement of a first foray in the European Cup Winner’s Cup, the club controversially doubled the usual £1 a seat and 50p standing tickets for the visit of Hungarian side Vasas Budapest.



A backlash led to a disappointing turnout of just 22,762 fans to see their side win the second leg 2-0 and advance in their first European game.

A price reduction for the next round worked. And 31,568 watched Sunderland beat Sporting Lisbon at Roker Park, though they were eventually eliminated after losing 2-0 in the return leg.

Murray, an accountant by trade but who made his fortune in kitchen manufacturing, may not have witnessed his heroes in Europe. But upon taking charge, he set out to get them back to the big time.

They came close on a hat-trick of occasions during his 20-year tenure. The first losing the 1992 FA Cup Final before back-to-back seventh place finishes at the turn of the century under Peter Reid’s legendary side.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Finally, this week he gets his wish. And the waterworks began when he spotted the current French-Swiss owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus at the Arsenal game.

Murray said: “I just walked up to the owners on Saturday and gave them a big hug and said, ‘Thank you.’ Simple as that. I’m in awe of them.

“My dad was a Sunderland coal miner. I used to come to the game with him. I’d get the service bus and Jackie White’s Market and get a saveloy. That’s what we did.

“Now I’ve booked tickets for Milan! Unbelievable, really. A few years ago, you’d never have seen this, would you?



“This is a one-off at the moment. I pinch myself about the whole thing, the profile for the city, everything.”

Murray has seen numerous owners come-and go since he sold up in 2006. As the club began to slide, he was even banned from attending games at one point by American Ellis Short after hitting out at the mis-management.

But even in those dark days his love for Sunderland never swayed. Murray founded the Foundation of Light and its award-winning home, the Beacon of Light, in the city. The award-winning community, education, and sports hub that provides local services and funds the Foundation of Light charity is about to celebrate its 25th anniversary.



And it was here that Murray remains hard at work trying to change the lives of others in the North East.

SUNDERLAND EURO MESSAGE Club statement Wednesday’s UEFA Europa League fixture against AZ Alkmaar will be a historic occasion for Sunderland AFC, marking the Club’s first European home fixture in 53 years. With supporters travelling from the Netherlands to experience the occasion, we are looking forward to welcoming AZ Alkmaar, its players and supporters to Sunderland and the Stadium of Light.

As part of their visit, a number of AZ Alkmaar supporters will take part in a planned march to the Stadium of Light. He says: “That’s been my privilege. I’ve done that through choice. I got out of bed and came here for a 12-hour day, and I want to do that. I don’t get money out of it. I’m very lucky and fortunate in life. Some people around here, not so fortunate.”

The Beacon of Light sits next to his other pride and joy – the Stadium of Light. He paid £25m, “not even enough to buy a full-back these days,” to build the ground in 1997.

It is somewhat of a drop-off having been named in the Ecuador squad for the World Cup, where he made one appearance.

So for the time being, the academy is the only platform on offer.

Sports.title: Premier League cult hero, 47, reveals he helped rescue Wrexham from oblivion before Ryan Reynolds takeover
Sports.content:
CRAIG BELLAMY has revealed how he once donated money to Wrexham to help save the Welsh club from dropping out of the Football League.

The Wales boss was defending his commitment to his country after revealing he rejected the chance to become Burnley manager this summer.



Bellamy said in a Wales press conference ahead of the upcoming Nations League matches: “I donated money to Wrexham (in 2007).

“They stayed in the league. So my commitment with Wales, I don’t believe I have to ever try and win anyone over with that. It’s there.”



Bellamy’s intervention came in March 2007, when Wrexham were second-bottom of League Two and fighting desperately to preserve their Football League status.

The then-Liverpool striker made what the club described as a “very generous donation,” with the exact sum never publicly disclosed.

The cash allowed Wrexham to bring in THREE loan players before the transfer deadline, and they stayed up.

Bellamy said at the time that, as a “proud Welshman and supporter of Welsh football”, it was important to him that Wrexham retained their Football League place.

His intervention helped them do exactly that, with the Red Dragons eventually surviving on the final day of the 2006-07 season.

But their reprieve proved temporary and Wrexham were relegated to non-league the following year.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

They spent a painful 15 YEARS outside the EFL before their fortunes were transformed by two unlikely figures from Hollywood.

Deadpool star Ryan Reynolds and It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia creator Rob McElhenney completed their takeover in February 2021, buying the club from the Wrexham Supporters Trust and initially investing £2million.

Their extraordinary project – chronicled around the world through hit documentary Welcome to Wrexham – eventually produced one of English football’s most remarkable rises.

Under boss Phil Parkinson, Wrexham won the National League with 111 points in 2023 to finally return to the Football League.

They did not stop there, earning promotion from League Two at the first attempt before finishing second in League One in 2024-25.



Wrexham narrowly missed out on the Championship play-offs in their first season back in the second tier and remain there this season.

Sports.title: DAZN host Diletta Leotta shows off curves in translucent top as fans say ‘what a lucky man Karius is’
Sports.content:
DILETTA LEOTTA delighted fans with her latest social media snaps.

And followers joked her goalkeeper husband Loris Karius is a very lucky man indeed.



The glamorous Italian DAZN presenter, 35, took to Instagram on Tuesday with a life update.

She posted 14 pictures and one video to her 9.4million followers.



And that included various revealing outfits.

The collection of snaps featured a mix of selfies, at work on and off screen, enjoying family time and even her collection of heels.

Diletta captioned the post: “A little bit of everything I love.”

And as well as racking up nearly 100,000 likes within 11 hours, more than 350 fans flooded the comments section.



One gushed: “Stunning as always.”

Another beamed: “Absolutely stunning, out of this world.”



A third typed: “You are so beautiful.”

A fourth declared: “Diletta Leotta you are perfect.”



And a final user quipped: “@loriskarius YOU ARE THE LUCKIEST MAN IN THE WORLD.”

Diletta, who has worked as a Serie A broadcaster with DAZN since 2018, married Karius in 2024 in Italy.

The ex-Liverpool stopper has two children with Diletta – daughter Aria and son Leonardo.

Sports.title: West Ham 2 Fulham 3: Oscar Bobb takes advantage of Kante error to hand Arbeloa’s strugglers morale-boosting win
Sports.content:
OSCAR BOBB burst West Ham’s bubbles as his 78th-minute winner sent Fulham through.

The second-half sub cashed in after Mo Kante lost possession on the edge of his box to fire past Finlay Herrick.



It was a boost for boss Alvaro Arbeloa on the back of Fulham’s first point of the season — in their fourth league game — at Liverpool.

Championship leaders West Ham twice pegged Fulham back in a thrilling first half.



The visitors took a 13th-minute lead when Rodrigo Muniz planted a header home after Cesar Palacios pulled the ball back.

But West Ham — fresh from beating Wrexham 6-0 on Friday — took just three minutes to level the tie.

Arne Engels’ deep cross was headed back into the danger zone by Konstantinos Mavropanos for Morato to head his first Hammers goal.

Rookie keeper Herrick, 20, then got down well to push a Palacios shot around the post.

But Fulham went route one to restore their lead in the 37th minute.

Joachim Andersen raked a ball forward for Palacios to run on to before shooting past Herrick.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Max Dowman, 16, draws Messi comparisons as Merino shows why Gyokeres has been frozen out
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’s B-team cruised into the fourth round of the League Cup as they brushed Ipswich Town aside in a 4-2 win.

Mikel Arteta made nine changes to his side that beat Sunderland at the weekend, but his heavily-rotated squad still looked like the business at Portman Road.



The Gunners were in control from the off as teen sensation Max Dowman opened the scoring after seven minutes with a terrific solo goal.

The teen sensation bagged a second later in the game alongside goals from Mikel Merino and Noni Madueke.



Arteta will have been chuffed with his team’s showing as they barely had to get out of second gear to find the result.

Here SunSport Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall rates each individual Arsenal performance…

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 6

The backup goalkeeper had little to do and will be disappointed not to have kept a clean sheet given Arsenal’s dominance.

MARLI SALMON – 7

A fifth senior appearance for the teenager, who signed his first professional deal last month on his 17th birthday.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Faced a serious battle against Zian Flemming, one that saw him struggle at times, but ultimately came out of it as the winner on the night.

He is so comfortable with the ball at his feet and even when he was almost caught in possession by Marcelino Nunez he had the confidence to get out of trouble and drive into midfield.

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 8

Made a crucial last-ditch tackle to deny a certain goal from Jaden Philogene.

The Brazilian acted as Salmon’s big brother for most of the game, guiding the teen through the game and sweeping up any little errors he made.

Subbed off at half-time to save his legs after a professional performance.



MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

Pushed back into the left-back position despite a great start to the season in midfield.

The 19-year-old slotted straight back into the role with ease and put in another confident performance.

MARTIN ZUBIMENDI – 7

Deployed as a makeshift right-back due to the absences of Ben White and Jurrien Timber.

The biggest compliment would be that it was hard to even tell he was playing in that position as he went about his night with minimal fuss. Assured performance.

BRUNO GUIMARAES – 8

A first start since the Community Shield for the Brazilian, off the back of his stunner off the bench against Sunderland.



His role in Arsenal’s second goal was superb, chasing down the back line like a man possessed to win the ball back high up the pitch.

He and Mikel Merino bossed the midfield behind Dowman to allow the teen to shine.

MIKEL MERINO – 8

The Spaniard was wearing the captain’s armband and put in a performance to match.



He was all over the pitch in his midfield role, dictating play and allowing the players around him to find space off the ball.

His delightful dinked ball into the path of Noni Madueke set up Arsenal’s second goal of the night, while his finish to find the bottom corner for the fourth was brilliant.

MAX DOWMAN – 9

Arteta warned Dowman that he must “earn” his minutes this week, after the 16-year-old was left out of the matchday squad for Sunderland at the weekend.

It took the teenager less than seven minutes to show the Arsenal boss exactly what he can do.

His opening goal was a moment of magic, leaving Cedric Kipre for dead with a cheeky shimmy and sending the keeper the wrong way with a tide finish too.



And he played a crucial role in the second goal too, pressing the goalkeeper to force the loose pass and allow Guimaraes to win the ball back.

His second goal was another example of how composed he is for his age, calmly tucking it into the bottom corner, while his dummy ‘assist’ for Merino’s fourth was another sparkling moment.

Arteta has previously compared Dowman to a young Lionel Messi, and it is genuinely not insane to do so when you see just how talented he is.



NONI MADUEKE – 7

It is fair to say Madueke has faced some criticism for his end product since joining Arsenal last summer, but his finish for the second goal was top tier.

If Madueke can make those moments a more regular feature of his game then his reputation in North London will improve tenfold.

EBERECHI EZE – 6

Back on the left wing, where he will likely play most of his football this season given Arsenal’s lack of depth in that position.

It wasn’t exactly an inspiring performance from the England international, who will have been hoping to bag a goal to show he can do it from out wide.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 5

The Swede has scarcely been given a chance up top so far this season, with Arteta preferring Kai Havertz to lead his line in every Premier League game.



This performance did little to change that as Gyokeres struggled to be involved in a match that Arsenal dominated once again.

Sports.title: Brook, Buttler go berserk again as England thrash Sri Lanka in first T20
Sports.content:
​​Harry Brook and Jos Buttler went berserk in a T20 at Southampton for the second time this summer as England smoked 254-4 against Sri Lanka during a 119-run win in the series opener - their first game since Kevin Pietersen's appointment as white-ball mentor.

White-ball captain Brook (114no off 49 balls) - who nailed six boundaries in one over - and predecessor in that role Buttler (80 off 44) plundered 128 from just 60 balls in partnership for England's second wicket once debutant Aneurin Donald (12 off 5) fell after slamming a six and a four amid a bright but fleeting cameo.

Brook and Buttler had combined for a riotous stand of 233 from 103 balls at the same venue in July as England romped to a total of 257-3 against India that secured a 4-0 series sweep, with Buttler tonking a century on that occasion and Brook an unbeaten 95.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The best of Brook's sensational 114 not out from just 49 balls in the first T20I against Sri Lanka in Southampton

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brook slammed 30 runs off one over with six successive boundaries off Sri Lanka spinner Dunith Wellalage

Score summary - England vs Sri Lanka, first T20, Southampton England 254-4 in 20 overs (put in to bat): Harry Brook (114no off 49 balls), Jos Buttler (80 off 44), Will Jacks (21 off 12); Wanindu Hasaranga (1-34) Sri Lanka 135 all out in 19 overs (target 255): Dunith Wellelage (33 off 21 balls), Dasun Shanaka (24 off 14), Eshan Malinga (13no off 5); Sonny Baker (3-12), Jamie Overton (2-20), Liam Dawson (2-23) , Will Jacks (1-21) Full scorecard Watch Thursday's second T20 in Cardiff live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 6pm (6.30pm first ball).

This time around the roles were reversed with Buttler - playing his first innings since the Hundred final at Lord's on August 16 - missing out on a ton but Brook reaching three figures for the second time in T20 internationals, doing so from just 42 deliveries as he mixed big hits with slick, intense running.

No wonder England legend Pietersen, who scored almost 14,000 runs in all international cricket between 2004 and 2014, was smiling throughout.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of the first T20, Sky Sports' Eoin Morgan and Kumar Sangakkara looked at what white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen will bring to the set-up

That expression continued as Sri Lanka subsided to 135 all out in 19 overs in reply, to suffer a 13th successive defeat to their opponents in this format, stretching back to 2014, and England made it 21 wins from their last 24 T20Is.

The pacey, accurate and economical Sonny Baker bagged 3-12 from four overs, including bowling Kamil Mishara (10) to claim his first white-ball wicket for England, while leg-spin maestro Adil Rashid (1-31) nicked off Dasun Shanaka (24 off 14) with a peach of a delivery having just been belted for back-to-back sixes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Sonny Baker took his first white-ball wicket for England by bowling Sri Lanka's Kamil Mishara.

KP watches on as Brook dazzles at Utilita Bowl

Brook's innings was a joy to watch, with his expert ability to pick up length on full display in the 30-run fifth over of the game when he struck Sri Lankan left-arm spinner Dunith Wellalage for six boundaries in as many deliveries (three sixes, three fours).

Brook's first boundary in that set, a six onto the cushion at long-on, was a little edgy but his next five were sublime - fours over the bowler's head and down to long-on, a scooped six over fine leg, a maximum over long-off and, finally, a four behind point.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Sky Sports pundit Stuart Broad's failed attempt to get an interview with Brook at the halfway stage at the Utilita Bowl

Only Phil Salt - missing this series due to a quad injury, hence why Derbyshire batter Donald has been handed a chance - has hit a faster T20I hundred for England than Brook, taking 39 balls against South Africa in 2025 when the team amassed 304-2 in Manchester.

Former England Test captain Ben Stokes took to social media to say: "I don't even think the genius of KP could come close to what Brook has talent-wise. You are an absolute freak, Harry. You're mint to watch."

Stokes would later add: "Bit harsh on KP actually. Both are freak talents but Brook is better in my opinion."

Welshman Donald will be looking to make a more sustained impact in the country of his birth in the second T20 - the 29-year-old came through the Glamorgan academy and is the Cardiff county's first homegrown international since 2005 Ashes hero Simon Jones.

After Donald heaved a maximum leg-side and drilled four through extra-cover next ball, he spooned Wellalage down the ground, before watching on as Brook and Buttler made mincemeat of the tourists' bowling attack - the duo spanking 28 boundaries between them.

"He was a phenomenal player. The way he accessed different areas of the ground made it really tricky to captain and bowl to, and I'm looking forward to conversations about that.

"Hopefully he can have a big impact on my career. He's a hero to a lot of players. We grew up watching him and it's just awesome to have a man of his calibre in the changing room."

Sports.title: Peterborough edge out Barnsley on penalties after six-goal thriller
Sports.content:
Peterborough moved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory over Barnsley that followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides.

Barnsley were gifted the lead after 61 seconds when Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar.

Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca's cross was pushed out by Barnsley goalkeeper Kieran Flavell as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in.

The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills' free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod.

But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner.

The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties by heading in Mills' cross with just two minutes remaining.

After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley's Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched.

Sports.title: Brentford hold off Reading to reach round four of Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Brentford emerged from a tense finish against Reading to book their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 2-1 victory at Select Car Leasing Stadium.

Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off.

Paudie O'Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading's challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off.

It took just 136 seconds for Brentford to take the lead with Wilson finding the bottom left corner of the net after a slip in defence by O'Connor turned Dango Ouattara's pass into an opportunity.

A cross by Carvalho caused problems in the visiting box and Reading then had the ball in the net but referee Tom Nield ruled out O'Connor's bicycle kick for a high boot.

O'Connor was doing everything possible to make up for his earlier mistake as he headed a free-kick inches over the crossbar.

Reading had clearly recovered from the shock of going behind so early as they poured forward, with a double clearance by Michael Kayode saving Brentford before Jamie Reid went desperately close.

O'Connor slipped again as he fluffed a clearance, giving Wilson time to pick his spot only for keeper Joel Pereira to get his body in the way.

Brentford scrambled to keep out Reid as he closed in on goal and then Conor Masterson flashed narrowly wide, but the Premier League club then scored on the counter-attack.

In a cruel blow for the Royals, Ouattara took advantage of the space in defence to slide the ball to Carvalho who calmly directed the ball beyond Pereira.

Ellery Balcombe's sharp reflexes prevented Josh Stokes from pulling one back for Reading but Brentford should have extended the lead only for Kayode to send a close-range effort wide.

Liam Fraser reminded the visitors they could not relax as he drilled a shot past the left post but the better chances were now coming at the other end, with Ouattara this time at fault for not making the most of a great opportunity.

Reading deserved a goal and it arrived in the 72nd minute when a corner was met by O'Connor's header, with the Irish defender's finish setting up a nervy finale.

On came Thiago but he was unable to improve the standard of finishing by his team, which had declined noticeably in the second half.

Sports.title: More talented than Pietersen? Brook brilliance leads to bold Stokes statement
Sports.content:
Ben Stokes no longer plays for England - but that has not stopped him from rating players who do or did.

Harry Brook is, in many ways, a modern-day Kevin Pietersen.

A player with jaw-dropping batting ability who can take any bowling attacking apart and make accessing any part of the ground look routine but also prone to driving fans mad with a daft dismissal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brook slammed 30 runs off one over with six successive boundaries off Sri Lanka spinner Dunith Wellalage

In Southampton on Tuesday, though, we only saw the best of Brook as he tonked a 42-ball hundred - England's second-fastest in T20Is - against Sri Lanka, with his 10 fours and half a dozen sixes including six boundaries in one over off Dunith Wellalage.

The swashbuckling innings was played in front of England legend Pietersen, who has joined head coach Brendon McCullum's white-ball set-up as a mentor, up to and including the 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe in late 2027.

And Brook's knock lured Stokes onto social media to say that, in his opinion, the Yorkshireman's ability outstrips that of Pietersen.

Brook still has a long way to go to match Pietersen longevity-wise.

KP amassed almost 14,000 international runs between 2004 and 2014, a number he was prevented from adding to after a fallout with the ECB truncated his England career.

Brook has over 6,500 international runs since debuting in 2022, so, all being well will eclipse Pietersen's haul at some stage.

At 27, he could have over a decade left - and he hopes to use Pietersen's expertise to become even better.

Image: Kevin Pietersen (right) is now a mentor to England's white-ball teams

Brook hopes 'hero' KP can have 'big impact' on his career

Brook said of Pietersen, after revealing he had watched highlights of his innings before Tuesday's T20: "He looked at batting slightly differently, in a similar way to me as well.

"He always wants to put the bowlers under pressure.

"He was a phenomenal player. The way he accessed different areas of the ground made it really tricky to captain and bowl to, and I'm looking forward to conversations about that.

"I mentioned to him earlier about trying to help me read surfaces and using my skills to perform on that pitch as well, not just for white-ball cricket, Test cricket as well.

"Hopefully he can have a big impact on my career. He's a hero to a lot of players. We grew up watching him and it's just awesome to have a man of his calibre in the changing room."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Eoin Morgan and Kumar Sangakkara heap praise on Brook following his century in Southampton

'Genius Brook has everything as a batter'

Brook's sizzling century against Sri Lanka was his first in any international cricket since a T20 ton versus Pakistan in February, during a World Cup match in Pallekele.

It was worth the wait. The batter's picking up of length was extraordinary in an innings highly praised by Sky Sports pundits Eoin Morgan and Kumar Sangakkara.

Sangakkara said of Brook: "He reads length so quickly. He is very light and nimble on his feet. He has oodles of time and devastating power. On the back foot against spin, he is very good at hitting over long-on, long-off, even square.

"Then against the pace there is the scoop and reverse paddle or punch down the ground for six. He has everything."

I feel like I've been there or thereabouts all summer, in all three formats. I feel like I've let myself down a couple of times - I've had the opportunity to score a big score. Thankfully I didn't give that opportunity up today. It was nice to get to three figures. A special feeling.

Morgan added: "I think Harry is one of our very best. It is difficult to find a player of recent generations that has Brook's ability.

"He is coming into his peak years, yet we are seeing absolute genius time and time again in all formats of the game."

Morgan is right about all formats, too.

Brook's last Test ton may have come over a year ago, against India at The Kia Oval, but he has knuckled down in red-ball matches of late, batting far more responsibly while notching five fifties across the summer in the international game's longest form.

In the international game's shortest form on Tuesday night, he did get a hundred - and how.

He can now chat about it with KP, a bloke he may even have more talent than…

Sports.title: Fulham edge West Ham in five-goal thriller
Sports.content:
Fulham came out on top of a thrilling London derby as they reached the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a 3-2 win over West Ham.

The visitors were pegged back twice at the London Stadium, but super-sub Oscar Bobb made the difference to hand Alvaro Arbeloa his second win as Cottagers boss.

Prior to the game, the Hammers held a period of appreciation in honour of former goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko, who passed away following a battle with cancer.

Image: Tomas Soucek carries a shirt to be laid behind a goal in tribute to former West Ham United player, Ludek Miklosko

West Ham had scored 27 goals this season prior to the tie, while Fulham had conceded three in two of their four Premier League games, so it was no surprise to see a goal-fest quickly commence.

After a dominant start, Rodrigo Muniz headed the visitors ahead after some lacklustre defending from the home side. However, that lead lasted less than three minutes, as some equally poor defending from a set-piece resulted in an easy header for Morato.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morato immediately cancels out Rodrigo Munoz's opener

Normal service continued after the equaliser, and having missed two good chances beforehand, Cesar Palacios finally applied the finishing touch with a classy poke past Finlay Herrick.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cesar Palacios nudges the ball past Finlay Herrick

Yet, in a case of deja vu, back came West Ham as Pablo smashed in his long-awaited first Hammers goal seconds before the break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pablo scored the fourth goal of the game

Both sides sent on the big guns in search of the winner. Jarrod Bowen and Taty Castellanos entered for the hosts, but it was Fulham's changes that made the difference. Josh King won possession on the edge of the West Ham box, before Bobb danced his way into the area and slotted home for his first goal for the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Bobb puts Fulham in front for a third time

The aforementioned West Ham duo combined for what surely had to be the equaliser as Bowen squared to Castellanos for a tap-in. However, the Spaniard was far too casual, allowing Timothy Castagne to clear off the line and ensure Fulham made it through.

Key moments from the London Stadium

13: GOAL! Muniz nods dominant Fulham in front.

16: GOAL! Morato with instant response as Fulham defend set piece poorly.

22: SAVE! Palacios works a shot well but Herrick equal to it.

36: WIDE! Palacios takes too long as he is crowded out while forcing a shot.

37: GOAL! Palacios finally gets his moment with a classy finish.

45 SAVE! Muniz should make it three, but sees his close-range effort saved by Herrick.

45+2: GOAL! What a time for Pablo to score his first West Ham goal as he smashes in rebound from Kante's flick.

65: WIDE! Mavropanos misses golden chance from corner.

77: GOAL! Bobb the hero as Norwegian scores his first goal for Fulham.

88: OFF THE LINE! Castellanos tap-in cleared away by Castagne.

90+3: WIDE! Palacios fails to kill the game off as he misses open goal.

Arbeloa calls for patience with youngsters

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa:

"We have so many young players with talent and we need to be patient with them.

"We need to help them, develop them, but you can see the talent they have, the quality. They understand the game and they will grow during the season."

On conceding twice:

"I'm so happy with the performance of my players and with the job that they did. We prepared well, we had a very good first half.

"I was a little bit upset at half-time. I'm still asking how we can concede these two goals. So easy, for me. We need to improve there. It's not easy for us to score goals; we need to do so many things well.

"We need to be a little bit more aggressive when we are defending. But everything that we worked on in the last two days, we did on the pitch."

Sports.title: Spurs do score but Szoboszlai stunner seals cup tie for Liverpool
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai’s stunning strike sealed a 3-1 win for Liverpool over Tottenham in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield.

Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo put the Reds in control before the hour but Conor Gallagher pulled one back for Roberto De Zerbi's team and it took a sensational fingertip save from Giorgi Mamardashvili to deny Omar Marmoush an equaliser.

There was no stopping Szoboszlai's stoppage-time effort, however, arrowed beyond Martin Dubravka. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool progress while the Spurs supporters have to be content with bagging their first goal of the campaign against top-flight opposition.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexis Mac Allister gave Liverpool the lead

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cody Gakpo scored with a powerful effort

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dominik Szoboszlai hits a thunderbolt to seal the victory

Key moments at Anfield

11 - SAVE! Bergvall kept out by the legs of Mamardashvili

21 - GOAL! Mac Allister curls the opener high into the net

32 - MISS! Kudus fails to find the target when well placed

54 - GOAL! Gakpo fires the ball home to double the lead

69 - GOAL! Gallagher nods the ball in from close range

86 - SAVE! Amazing by Mamardashvili to deny Marmoush

90+1 - GOAL! Szoboszlai's stunner seals it for the Reds

Lucas Bergvall really should have slotted Spurs in front early in the game but his close-range shot found the legs of Mamardashvili instead. And Liverpool punished them for that wastefulness when Mac Allister curled the ball high into the net for the opener.

Mohammed Kudus contrived to volley high and wide after smart work by Destiny Udogie before half-time. Liverpool were just more clinical, summed up by the manner in which Gakpo slammed in a second in front of the Kop to cap an excellent Liverpool move.

The Dutchman was a target for Tottenham in the summer. He currently has more Premier League goals this season than they do. Out of the Carabao Cup and with Richarlison out of the squad, De Zerbi's only consolation was a spirited effort at Anfield.

For Andoni Iraola, he will be encouraged by the energy and the quality in evidence. Intensity appeared to be an issue against Fulham on Saturday but the 10 changes actually helped with Lewis Koumas eager and Trey Nyoni producing a mature display in midfield.

And when Szoboszlai can do that, it makes everything easier.

Iraola: Szoboszlai goal a 'worldie'

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola speaking in the press conference:

"Three goals we scored were very good goals; the origin of the goals for the first and second ones was also very important for us. The third one is a worldie. With other players you are thinking it is too far. With Dom you are thinking he might score."

Player of the match: Lewis Koumas

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola speaking about Lewis Koumas in the press conference:

"I said in the week and say it for a reason; I see it in training every day. The energy that he shows is contagious for the rest. When they see the ones up front doing it, they are forced to go from behind."

Analysis: Positives for both teams

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp on Liverpool:

"That's the best I've seen them. Obviously, Tottenham played into their hands as they're trying to play out from the back. But the number of times they (Liverpool) won it back because they were so quick and aggressive to get after them. That's what Andoni did at Bournemouth and that's what he's trying to do at Liverpool. It will take time, but they'll certainly get it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Conor Gallagher scored Tottenham Hotspur's only goal of the night against Liverpool

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp on Tottenham:

"From Tottenham's point of view, there were positives. They had a sharpness to their game. Bergvall did well. There's lots to look forward to for the weekend. It was a better performance. On another day, they could have had two or three goals. Liverpool just had enough."

De Zerbi: We need things to click

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi speaking to Sky Sports:

"We created chances to win the game. It's not a very good moment, but I believe in my players, and I told them five minutes ago to stay calm.

"We need a click. I don't know if we are able to make this click Saturday, but playing like this and believing in ourselves and our style of play, I think we'll win many games and score many goals because the qualities of my players is very high.

"There are many, many positives. We are sorry, disappointed and frustrated for the results. I think we didn't deserve to lose, but it's the first season. We are building totally different things with me.

"I believe in my players, this project. I have no doubts. I believe in this club, but now we are not so lucky. It's not good to say too many 'ifs' but we played very well this evening."

Sports.title: Lincoln win at Bristol City to haunt old boss Skubala
Sports.content:
Bristol City boss Michael Skubala suffered defeat at the hands of his former club as Freddie Draper's second-half goal proved enough to give Lincoln a 1-0 Championship victory.

The decisive moment came on 53 minutes when Ben House intercepted Rob Dickie's miscued back-pass, which left goalkeeper Sam Tickle stranded, and set up Draper to shoot into an unguarded net.

The home side fought hard to level but Lincoln, promoted under Skubala last season, defended strongly to show how well they have adapted to life at the higher level.

Bristol City gave a home debut to 22-year-old Dutch midfielder Gibson Yah as one of three changes to the team beaten 4-1 at Southampton, while Lincoln made five changes from their 1-0 victory at Preston including a first League start for Chiedozie Ogbene supporting lone striker Draper.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robert Dickie sells his goalkeeper a pass that is too short as Lincoln's Freddie Draper is straight to the loose ball and finishes it into an empty net.

All the meaningful action in a competitive first half that saw five players cautioned came in the opening half-hour. Lincoln were first to threaten when Draper's low drive on four minutes was parried by Tickle.

Yu Hirakawa had a similar effort dealt with by Lincoln keeper George Wickens two minutes later before Bristol City came within inches of taking an 11th-minute lead.

Rio Cardines went into the match with five assists already this season and his pinpoint corner from the left saw Lorent Tolaj direct a powerful header against the crossbar.

Yah had a header deflected for a corner and Tolaj sliced wide at the far post from another Cardines cross before Lincoln went close on 27 minutes, Ogbene nodding wide at the near post after referee Tim Robinson had played a good advantage.

From then until the break, both sides struggled to create openings as the yellow card count mounted.

Draper's goal rewarded Lincoln for a bright start to the second half that saw Deji Elerewe glance a header wide while Ogbene had a low shot saved.

Draper fired over from distance with his team well on top and Lincoln fans taunting their former manager. But it took an outstretched leg from keeper George Wickens to protect the Imps' lead when Hirakawa was presented with a great chance on the hour.

Skubala had just replaced Jed Wallace with Dom Ballard in a bid to add potency up front.

Dickie's night to forget was ended by injury on 72 minutes, Rob Atkinson taking over as his fellow centre-back was stretchered off following a challenge from behind.

Bristol built some pressure and Yah's close-range shot was blocked following another Cardines corner.

The best the hosts could offer after that was an injury time effort from Ballard that passed harmlessly wide and home supporters were quick to voice their frustration at the final whistle.

The managers

Bristol City's Michael Skubala:

"We were not good enough tonight. We dealt well with their physicality, but in the second half we didn't create enough.

"I have only seen Rob Dickie for a matter of seconds, but he says he felt something give as he twisted and, while we don't know the extent of the damage yet, it looks a bad one affecting knee and ankle.

"I will go and see him again now and I expect he will go to hospital.

"We have gifted them their goal, no doubt about that. Playing out that way was unnecessary and it has cost us.

"We have only three days to wait for another home game, against Watford, and I think that is a good thing. We have to be better in that match."

Lincoln's Chris Cohen:

"No one has done more than Michael to put us where we are today and we wish him nothing but the best in his job with Bristol City.

"First and foremost I want to send my best wishes to Rob Dickie. Having had serious injuries myself, it is the last thing I want to see happen to any player.

"Things are going well for us so far in the Championship, but we know there are many tough days ahead. What I know is that the character and resilience we have built with Michael's help will help us at those times.

"It is pleasing that we have been able to change our back line and still keep a clean sheet. But the character shown on the pitch comes not only from the team and coaches, but everyone associated with our club, not least the supporters.

"We want to give them special memories, whether they have been fans for one year or fifty."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Middlesbrough battle back for point but miss chance to go top
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough missed out on the chance to climb to the top of the Sky Bet Championship despite coming from behind to earn a 2-2 draw with Millwall.

The Lions deservedly led by two goals at the break after capitalising on Boro's unconvincing start.

Strike duo Tairyk Arconte and Lyndon Dykes put Millwall in the driving seat after finding the net in the 11th and 36th minutes respectively.

But Middlesbrough, who controlled possession for most of the game, recovered to claim a point after head coach Kim Hellberg made three changes at half-time.

The excellent Amario Cozier-Duberry scored his second goal since arriving on loan from Brighton in the 50th minute, before striker Will Lankshear headed in his eighth of the season to equalise just after the hour.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Will Lankshear puts Middlesbrough level against Millwall with well-timed header at the back post after a good cross from Luke Ayling finds him.

That result lifted Middlesbrough to third place, despite breaking their 100 per cent home record.

Millwall took the early lead when Arconte, signed from French Ligue 2 side Rodez in the summer, darted past Luke Ayling before cutting back and striking low in off Radek Vitek's near post.

The 22-year-old's third goal of the season seemed the perfect response to Millwall's recent away slump, which had seen them concede eight goals on their last two trips.

Hellberg's side controlled most of the play after that opener, forcing Millwall to defend strongly.

Middlesbrough's closest chance in the opening half-hour was when Max Crocombe turned Lankshear's scrappy back-post volley over the bar.

But Middlesbrough looked threatened by the presence of Arconte and Dykes.

After conceding a corner just before half-time, the home side found themselves two goals down after failing to clear the ball into the box.

Jenson Metcalfe's delivery was met by Derek Mazou-Sacko's downward header, which Caleb Taylor flicked back across goal for Dykes, left out of new coach Sebastien Pocognoli's first Scotland squad, to turn in.

Hellberg disliked what he saw and introduced substitutes Kyle Joseph, Max Arfsten and Jeremy Sarmiento for the second half.

Within minutes Crocombe had to dive to his right to save a curling effort from Cozier-Duberry that energised the home fans.

Cozier-Duberry did not wait long for a goal. After Millwall failed to deal with a corner effectively, the London-born trickster's deflected effort hit the net.

Middlesbrough had lift-off. Just after the hour Lankshear headed in Ayling's deep cross to the back post to level the score.

Yet Vitek still had to make a point-blank save to stop substitute Elkan Baggott from heading Millwall back in front.

After that, the question was whether Middlesbrough would win it. Cozier-Duberry had a couple of chances, while Sarmiento curled an effort just wide of the upright as Millwall survived with a point.

The managers

Middlesbrough's Kim Hellberg:

"It was a weird game because they didn't create many chances but scored two in the first half, and we were not doing things we want to; it was below our standard and this game was on me.

"Amario was the best player in the first half, continued second half, you can see the quality he has. I am very happy with him, but we are putting ourselves in tough situations.

"In the first half we were below our standard, energy-wise and in general, but the group keeps showing the character they have is very strong; to come from two goals down and create chances, which we have done since we started the season.

"I had a lot of players who did brilliantly against Norwich, who maybe didn't have the energy tonight. I got some decisions wrong, that's on me."

Millwall's Alex Neil:

"There are very few times that I would say I'd take a point before the game because I set out to win every game, but after the last two away results we had to set out to be hard to beat.

"Normally we would deal with the goals we have conceded tonight, but I can't fault the lads for their effort.

"From our perspective, we came here to stodge the game up, hit on the counter.

"Everyone connected with Millwall knows we are down to the bare bones, we have 14 injuries, and I have to try to give the lads the best chance to win a game.

"There was a long time left on the clock after (the equaliser); we had to rally."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Szoboszlai screamer seals Liverpool’s progress as De Zerbi’s Spurs woes grow
Sports.content:
Tottenham scored and Roberto De Zerbi eulogised the quality at his disposal, yet try telling Spurs’ suffering away support there was consolation to be found at Anfield. Liverpool toyed with De Zerbi by advancing into round four with a quality of finishing that he can only dream of.

While the Spurs head coach talked a good game and his players played a pretty one in harmless areas, Liverpool produced the only effective one. Alexis Mac Allister promoted his claims for a new contract for the second midweek in succession with an excellent strike and Cody Gakpo continued his fine early season form with a smart second plus an assist. But both were overshadowed by Dominik Szoboszlai’s stupendous 25-yard finish in stoppage time.

“It was a worldie,” said Liverpool’s head coach, Andoni Iraola, whose changes injected energy and bite into the home display. “The thing with Dom is you trust him to score before he shoots. With others you might think it’s too far out, but not with him.”

Spurs caused a few anxieties when Conor Gallagher headed home after Giorgi Mamardashvili’s failure to deal with a Mateus Fernandes corner. But the Liverpool stand-in keeper atoned with several impressive stops, the best from Omar Marmoush, and the visitors’ wastefulness would prove another factor in their downfall. Defeat was deserved, despite De ­Zerbi’s claims to the contrary.

“We have to shoot more, we have to shoot better and we have to finish better the clear situations,” said the Spurs head coach. “But we are sorry for the result, disappointed, frustrated. I think it is unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments. In these five or six games we have not been lucky. We have to improve a lot of things but we are in the right way. I have big confidence and a big opinion of my players.”

View image in fullscreen Giorgi Mamardashvili clutches the ball as Destiny Udogie runs by. Photograph: Jon Super/AP

De Zerbi made eight changes from Saturday’s stalemate with Everton, Iraola made 10 from a similarly drab draw against Fulham. It was new faces but a similar story for Spurs as, for the second successive game against Merseyside opposition, they seized control from the start but failed to capitalise when in the ascendancy. Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus both should have scored from left-wing crosses by Destiny Udogie. The former allowed Mamardashvili to make an ­important, improvised save when he had the entire goal to aim for. The latter volleyed over from four yards out.

Liverpool turned the tide thanks to impressive contributions from the young quartet of Lewis Koumas, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha. Koumas led the line with an aggression and work rate that Iraola wants from all of his forwards, regardless of their price tags.

Mac Allister opened the scoring when Udogie’s attempt to halt Ngumoha’s weaving run across the area put the ball on a plate for the incoming midfielder. Opening his body, Mac Allister went for power and placement and swept a shot into Martin Dubravka’s top left-hand corner.

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s Alexis Mac Allister fires past Martin Dubravka to open the scoring. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Mac Allister’s opener arrived between Spurs’ two missed chances from Bergvall and Kudus. Another fine Liverpool move and emphatic finish punished the visitors a second time nine minutes after the restart. McConnell and Ngumoha were heavily involved before Milos Kerkez picked out Mac Allister in space, prompting groans from the Kop over the full-back’s refusal to shoot. They were quickly silenced as the Argentina international’s first-time pass found Gakpo, who stepped inside a nonexistent challenge from Archie Gray and beat Dubravka with an angled drive.

All hope appeared to have been lost for Spurs, not that their finishing offered much in the first place, but the stoic backing of their admirable away support indicated ­otherwise. The visitors were handed a lifeline when Mamardashvili and Jeremie Frimpong failed to deal with a Fernandes corner. The goalkeeper missed his attempt to punch clear and Gallagher, left alone at the back post by Frimpong, had the simple task of heading in from close range.

Quick Guide Roundup: Bass and Jones Peterborough's shootout heroes Show Peterborough moved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory over Barnsley that followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides. Barnsley were handed the lead after 61 seconds when a clearance by the Peterborough goalkeeper, Alex Bass, was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar. Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca’s cross was pushed out by the Barnsley goalkeeper, Kieran Flavell, as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in. The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills’ free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod. But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner. The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties with by heading in Mills’ cross with just two minutes remaining. After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley’s Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched. Brentford emerged from a tense finish against Reading to book their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 2-1 victory. Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off. Paudie O’Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading’s challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although the substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Mamardashvili made amends in superb style to deny Marmoush an equaliser when the forward’s shot took a slight deflection off ­Ronald Araújo. At the other end Tosin Adarabioyo escaped twice: first with a wayward pass that led to a gilt-edged chance for Szoboszlai, saved by Dubravka, and when Alexander Isak’s cross struck his arm. There was no video assistant referee in operation to correct the decision.

Spurs would not escape a third time. In stoppage time, Szoboszlai let Gakpo’s flick roll off his chest before thumping a fabulous shot beyond Dubravka from long range. He celebrated by pointing to his ear, perhaps in response to the criticism his display against Fulham had attracted. The Liverpool vice-captain’s concerns pale in comparison to De Zerbi’s and his toothless team.

Sports.title: Max Dowman doubles up for Arsenal’s back-ups to beat Ipswich in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
The bad news for everyone else is that Arsenal’s next generation is already here. Two mesmerising goals and an assist in a man-of-the-match display from Max Dowman underlined why the 16-year-old has been compared to a certain Lionel Messi by his manager, Mikel Arteta, as Ipswich were swatted aside with ease. Almost as impressive was the performance of the 17-year-old Marli Salmon, who oozed class in central defence on only the second senior start of his career.

Ipswich won here the last time these two sides met in this competition, in 2011, but were beaten 3-0 in the second leg of the semi-final at the Emirates before Arsenal infam­ously lost to Birmingham in the final. ­Fifteen years on, Gary O’Neil’s heavily rotated side stood no chance against last year’s runners up after Dowman’s brilliant opening goal. Noni Madueke and the stand-in skipper Mikel Merino were also on target as Arsenal made it seven wins out of seven to start the new campaign. Having finally ended their long wait for silverware in style, this team are hungry for more and know they can now rely on one of the most exciting talents ever to have emerged from their Hale End academy.

“He can deliver those actions effortlessly. That’s his biggest quality,” said Arteta of the delightful shimmy that preceded Dowman’s first goal. “It’s a joy to have him. But what we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context. We really need to make sure every time we throw him in, he’s in the right context with the right ­preparation. That’s what we are ­trying to do.”

Both managers made their prior­ities clear as there were a combined 19 changes from their sides’ wins in the Premier League at the weekend. After a summer of heavy spending, many of those who helped Ipswich bounce straight back from the Championship last season were given an opportunity to stake a claim but largely failed to do so. “It’s the most extreme test that you can face,” admitted O’Neil. “Every time we made a mistake we were punished.”

Dowman’s most recent first-team appearance was in the final game of last season when Arsenal were crowned champions, and he has since completed his GCSEs before spending a week in New York during the World Cup where he rubbed shoulders with Paul Pogba.

Arteta said beforehand he would have “earn his minutes” like anyone else and it only took seven of them for Dowman to seize his opportunity. Ipswich’s fans were taunting their Arsenal counterparts about never being crowned European champions when he muscled Santiago Núñez off the ball on the halfway line and set off towards the penalty area. The imposing figure of Cédric Kipré – all 6ft 3in of him – was all that stood in Dowman’s way but he went past the Ivory Coast defender in a flurry of feet before cooly dispatching a shot into the corner and performing a Thierry Henry knee slide for good measure.

Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca’s cross was pushed out by the Barnsley goalkeeper, Kieran Flavell, as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in. The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills’ free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod. Ipswich’s mission got even harder when Madueke hammered in after Bruno Guimarães and Merino had combined to set him up after Dowman had started the press. Barely a quarter of an hour had been played. To their credit, the hosts rallied and it needed a clearance off the line from Salmon to deny Zian Flemming. Not to be outdone by Dowman, Salmon – who signed his professional contact when he turned 17 last month having also played in the Champions League and FA Cup last season – set out on a slaloming run just before half-time after calmly turning his way out of trouble under pressure from Flemming, drawing a round of applause from the Arsenal bench.

View image in fullscreen The former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom scores Ipswich’s second goal. Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images

Ipswich’s hopes of mounting a comeback were extinguished within two minutes of the restart when Dowman struck again. Martín Zubimendi’s pass found him on the edge of the six-yard box and the finish was caressed into the far corner. Merino then curled home off the post from Dowman’s touch to put the result beyond any doubt, although the biggest roar of the evening came when Ipswich hit back through Anis Mehmeti after he was set up by the substitute Jack Clarke.

Including Myles Lewis-Skelly – a relative veteran these days at 19 and surely in line for an England recall this week after an excellent start to the season – Arsenal had four teenagers on the pitch at the end after the 18-year-old Theo Julienne came on at right-back. Even Ipswich had a Hale End grad­uate in their ranks by then as Chuba Akpom grabbed another consolation in injury time via a deflection. But, not for the last time one suspects, it was Dowman’s name that was on everyone’s lips at the end.

Sports.title: Oscar Bobb takes Fulham past stubborn West Ham and into Carabao Cup last 16
Sports.content:
Álvaro Arbeloa played in some great defences but whether he knows how to coach one remains to be seen. ­Fulham have been fragile since appointing the Spaniard and they were fortunate not to be dragged into a penalty shootout by West Ham as this entertainingCarabao Cup tie drew to a close.

West Ham equalised twice during the first half and they almost did it again after Oscar Bobb made it 3-2 in the 78th minute. Nuno Espírito Santo raged at a poor miss from Taty ­Castellanos, though, and Fulham clambered into the last 16 after resisting late pressure from the ­Championship pacesetters.

It was a mixed bag as far as ­Fulham were concerned. West Ham were beaten but not outplayed and will not mind switching focus back to their promotion push. They stretched Fulham. Arbeloa played an experimental lineup and the performance was not convincing. César Palacios finished with a goal and an assist but Kevin and Emile Smith Rowe disappointed and the Premier League side needed Bobb and Josh King to make the difference after coming off the bench.

“I was a bit upset at half-time,” Arbeloa said. “I am asking how we can concede these two goals. So easy for me. We need to improve there. We need to be more aggressive when defending. In the end we need a massive save. If we are not aggressive enough it is my job to improve my players. We have to work a lot.”

Before kick-off there was a moving tribute to Ludek Miklosko, the legendary former West Ham goalkeeper, after he passed away this week at the age of 64. It added emotion to the tie, ensuring the hosts were not short of motivation against the hardest side they have faced since last season’s relegation.

Although West Ham rested key players in attack before visiting ­Millwall on Saturday they responded well after going behind in the 13th minute. They tested Fulham in the air and levelled when Arne Engels’ deep cross found Konstantinos Mavropanos, who rose at the far post and headed across for his fellow defender Morato to nod in his first goal since joining from Nottingham Forest on loan this month.

View image in fullscreen Pablo made it 2-2 just before half-time but West Ham could not find a winner after the break. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

It was frustrating for the visitors not to maintain control after Palacios darted down the left before picking out Rodrigo Muniz, who headed in the opener after creeping between Mavropanos and Maximilian Kilman.

Fulham’s grip remained tentative. Arbeloa had gambled by making nine changes, a risky move after calming the noise around his position with Saturday’s draw at Liverpool. The lead was regained in style, Joachim Andersen’s pass from deep allowing Palacios to wander through a big gap and poke past Finlay Herrick, but Fulham were not resilient enough. Their pressing was uncoordinated and it was 2-2 when Benjamin Lecomte’s save from Mohamadou Kanté’s flick ran to Pablo, who marked his 22nd appearance for West Ham by scoring his first goal since joining for £18.3m last January.

Quick Guide Roundup: Bass and Jones Peterborough's shootout heroes Show Peterborough moved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory over Barnsley that followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides. Barnsley were handed the lead after 61 seconds when a clearance by the Peterborough goalkeeper, Alex Bass, was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar. Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca’s cross was pushed out by the Barnsley goalkeeper, Kieran Flavell, as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in. The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills’ free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod. But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner. The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties with by heading in Mills’ cross with just two minutes remaining. After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley’s Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched. Brentford emerged from a tense finish against Reading to book their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 2-1 victory. Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off. Paudie O’Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading’s challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although the substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off. With the game in the balance Nuno made a bold move by introducing Jarrod Bowen and Manor Solomon early in the second half. Fulham drifted. Antonee Robinson drew a save from Herrick but Solomon and Mavropanos went close for West Ham.

Arbeloa threw on Bobb, King and Gonzalo García. West Ham tired and King was alert when Kanté dithered in a dangerous position. The Fulham youngster pressed to win possession, leaving Bobb to cut in from the right and drill a low shot past Herrick.

West Ham kept going. Bowen shot over and Castellanos, on for Pablo, had an effort cleared off the line by Timothy Castagne. Fulham lived on the edge.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling could face prison for reckless driving while using nitrous oxide
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and could be sent to prison after driving his ­Lamborghini for more than an hour on motorways during rush hour while inhaling nitrous oxide.

The former Chelsea and Manchester City forward stood in the dock to accept three charges before ­Basingstoke magistrates court heard how he embarked on a ­prolonged period of reckless driving on the M25 and M3, inhaling nitrous oxide ­balloons, before crashing his £270,000 car. Sterling was disqualified from driving and bailed until 25 November, when his sentence will either be determined or referred to the crown court.

Sterling also admitted possession of nitrous oxide and refusing to ­provide a specimen.

The maximum term for Sterling would be two years in prison, although a sentence of 12 to 18 months is considered more likely and, with mitigation, that could be suspended.

Simon Jones, prosecuting, told the court one witness had “genuine concerns the driver might kill someone” and described Sterling’s driving as “absolutely horrendous”.

“As she moved past the vehicle she thought the airbag had been deployed, it was a large white deflated balloon,” Jones said. “She had no idea if the driver could see ahead.”

View image in fullscreen Raheem Sterling (centre) arriving at Basingstoke magistrates court on Tuesday. Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PA

Between 7.45am and 8.52am on 28 May, police received multiple calls reporting dangerous driving – shortly after Sterling had returned to England after a loan at Feyenoord, where he had attempted to revive his career.

Dashcam footage provided to police by one witness showed Sterling’s car swerving between lanes and almost colliding with the central reservation. Witnesses reported seeing the driver inhaling balloons while driving.

After leaving the M3, the Lamborghini veered off the carriageway on the A327 near the Minley interchange in Hampshire. All four tyres blew out and there was damage to the bodywork. Body-worn footage from officers attending the scene, played in court, showed Sterling, 31, sitting in the passenger seat with two canisters on his lap before confirming he had been driving.

Jones said Sterling appeared keen to move a deflated balloon from beside him on to the back seat. His saliva was tested and no presence of cannabis or cocaine was found, but he later refused to provide a blood sample to test for other substances.

Quick Guide How do I 

Another witness told police they had seen the Lamborghini driving erratically at 1.10am. They reported it entering a drive-through at “alarming speed”, Jones said, and saw the driver holding an inflated balloon.

After his arrest, Sterling was taken to Basingstoke investigation centre. “During the process he had disclosed to staff that he had a problem with nitrous oxide,” Jones said.

Sterling failed a series of impairment tests, including walking in a straight line without swaying and placing his fingertip on the end of his nose. He was also asked to judge 30 seconds with his eyes closed but recorded 52.

Jones said Sterling “appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting” during the tests. “His eyelids were drooping, consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.”

The former England international, who won 82 caps between 2012 and 2022 and played in five major tournaments, was taken to a medical room where he refused to provide a blood sample without providing a reasonable excuse and despite repeated and clear warnings.

At 5.13pm, Sterling was interviewed with a legal representative present. A signed, prepared statement was read out in which he said he had not slept all night and was tired and confused. He then answered “no comment” to officers’ questions.

Jason Bartfield KC for the defence did not dispute this was a top-category case, given the prolonged driving and clear serious impairment. Bartfield cautioned, however, that there would have been “short periods” of “serious impairment”, compared with consuming cannabis or alcohol.

View image in fullscreen Raheem Sterling after being stopped by police in May. Photograph: Crown Prosecution Service/PA

Bartfield did not accept the car damage was serious, describing it as “relatively superficial” and “minor scratching” alongside the blown tyres. He also argued that the fact there were two canisters in Sterling’s lap when police arrived showed “this was very much not a case of trying to conceal anything from them”.

The court was not told the full mitigating circumstances, but ­Bartfield said: “Clearly there is extensive ­personal mitigation. Voluntary steps have been taken to address them. I hope this has weight with the court.”

District judge Kirsty Allman ordered a pre-sentence report and adjourned the hearing. She said she had not decided whether to retain jurisdiction or commit sentencing to the crown court. A magistrates court cannot impose a sentence of more than 12 months.

“I’m going to release you on unconditional bail,” she said. “If you don’t attend, a warrant will be issued for your arrest. I’m going to disqualify you from driving as of today. You must not drive a motor vehicle on the road as of today. I will determine the period if I sentence you, otherwise it will be for the crown court. You must not drive while disqualified – if you drive while disqualified you will be committing a prisonable offence.”

Sports.title: Manchester United shocked as talented youngster JJ Gabriel asks to leave
Sports.content:
Manchester United have been left confused and shocked by the news that the talented 15-year-old player JJ Gabriel has asked to leave the club, a day before he was to be included in the first-team squad to face Brighton.

Gabriel could have become United’s youngest player in the Carabao Cup third-round tie at Old Trafford on Wednesday. But the Guardian understands he has asked for his registration to be cancelled.

United are unsure what has prompted this decision and believe they have done everything they can to show Gabriel and his family there is a pathway to the first team. Those efforts have included meetings with Ruben Amorim, when the Portuguese was head coach, and Sir Alex Ferguson.

United believe the situation, first reported by the Telegraph, is rectifiable given the time remaining on Gabriel’s contract. Club officials say the player has a deal to the end of the season and cannot be deregistered despite his request. The north London-born Gabriel cannot sign a professional contract until he turns 17 in October next year, but can sign a scholarship agreement when he turns 16.

Gabriel, who has been with United since the age of 11, has emerged as one of the most exciting prospects at Carrington in years, scoring a hatful of goals for the youth teams, most recently a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut against Sabah last week. He regularly plays for older age groups at United, scoring 26 goals in 29 games last season, and has made two appearances for England Under-17s. Gabriel is also the most recent, and youngest, winner of United’s prestigious Jimmy Murphy young player of the year award. He has regularly trained with the first team.

Quick Guide Carrick say VAR blunder will fuel United Show Michael Carrick believes Manchester United will have an edge against Brighton in the Carabao Cup owing to the wrong video assistant referee decision that allowed Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s defeat by Manchester City. United host Fabian Hürzeler’s side on Wednesday aiming to bounce back after Haaland’s 60th-minute strike was judged to be legal by the VAR, who ruled that Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup. Pro Ref admitted the goal should not have been allowed and that Matt Donohue, the VAR, had made the wrong decision. He has been stood down for this weekend's Premier League action. Carrick, speaking before Pro Ref’s statement, was asked whether his players would have an edge against Brighton owing to their annoyance at ruling. “It does give you something, when something like that happens, to use moving forward," the manager said. "The players have got an edge. They've shown that to me since I've been here. We've had setbacks, and they've bounced back particularly well and had some really good performances and good results." United have taken four points from their first four games. “We've got to move on [from City loss]; we've got to win games,” said Carrick. “We have done – we've won a lot of games, and we need to continue to do that. I understand it's a new season, and the points tally right now is not what we want it to be. I'm not hiding from that, but it's more of about getting back to winning games, that feeling, getting the habit. It's easier said than done, but we're capable of it.” Luke Shaw may be available after a knock. Jamie Jackson Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Speaking after that 5-0 win against Sabah, Adam Lawrence, United’s lead under-21 coach, said: “JJ is surrounded by people that really, really believe in him from the top of the club right the way through. He’s been at the club for so long. He’s got real good relationships with the players, with the staff, so I think over the course of time obviously that helps as well.

“At the moment, just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, it’s about making sure that he’s getting the right exposure across different levels. We’re obviously not perfect but it’s definitely something we put a lot of thought into.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi called up by Argentina to make farewell ⁠appearance in friendly
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has been called up by Argentina to make a farewell ⁠appearance in a home friendly in October following his international retirement, the Argentinian football association (AFA) has confirmed.

“We invited ⁠the best player in ⁠the world ​to play, the icon of our selection, our captain Lionel Andrés Messi, to have a deserved farewell on 6 October, here in Argentina,” the AFA president, Claudio Tapia, said on social media.

Argentina will play three home friendlies during the 21 September to 6 October Fifa international window, their first matches since the World Cup.

They will take on ​Benin in Buenos Aires’ Monumental ‌Stadium on 6 October, ‌where Messi, who announced his retirement from international football last month, has been invited ‌to play his farewell match.

Quick Guide Rodríguez retires from international football Show Colombia midfielder James Rodríguez retired from international football on ⁠Tuesday, having won 131 caps and inspired his country to the 2014 ⁠World Cup ⁠quarter-finals. “Thank ​you for every match, every joy, every tear and every dream we ⁠shared. Defending the colours of the Colombia national team was one of the ⁠greatest honours of my life,” Rodríguez said in ​a video posted ‌on social media. The ‌35-year-old, who made his senior debut in 2011 ‌and often captained Colombia, scored 31 goals and represented his country at three World Cups and four Copa América tournaments. Rodríguez rose to global prominence at the 2014 World Cup in ‌Brazil, scoring six goals to win the Golden Boot as Colombia reached the ​quarter-finals. His volley against Uruguay in the last 16 earned him Fifa’s Puskas Award for the best goal of the year. He signed for Colombian ⁠side Atlético Nacional last week on a deal ​running ​until next June after ​leaving Major League Soccer club Minnesota ​United. Was this helpful? Argentina will also face Bolivia at Córdoba’s Mario Kempes Stadium on 30 September before moving to Buenos Aires to host Burkina Faso on 3 October. The Bolivia match will be played with capacity reduced by 50% as part of Fifa’s sanctions relating to incidents during this year’s ‌World Cup.

“Footballers Messi, [Rodrigo] De Paul and [Giovani] Lo Celso will be in attendance to take part in the final friendly on 6 October. ​Meanwhile, the names of the players called up from the local league will be announced on Friday,” the AFA said in a statement announcing the squad.

Sports.title: Howard Webb says accidental handball law ‘a nonsense’ and calls for reform
Sports.content:
Howard Webb has described the law around accidental handball as “a bit of a nonsense” and called for its reform to stop referees being drawn into “ridiculous situations”.

The chief refereeing officer for English football made his remarks on Tuesday, when he also fronted up over the error that allowed Manchester City to win Sunday’s Manchester derby. Webb said he was “really disappointed” with the video assistant referee call that failed to spot Enzo Fernández interfering with play from an offside position before Erling Haaland scored the only goal.

Speaking on Match Officials Mic’d Up, Webb reviewed a number of controversial incidents from the Premier League season. He said the buildup to an Ipswich own goal at Manchester United, where the ball hit Harry Maguire’s hand before he took a shot that deflected off Jacob Greaves and into the net, highlighted problems with the handball law.

“It’s a bit of a nonsense, isn’t it?” Webb said. “If [Maguire] strikes the ball beautifully into the top corner, then the goal gets disallowed. [But] he skews his shot, it becomes an own goal, and it’s awarded.”

The handball law says it is an offence “if a player scores in the opponent’s goal directly from their hand/arm [or] immediately after the ball has touched their hand/arm, even if accidental”. If another player touches the ball before it goes in, however, only a deliberate handball would lead to play being brought back. Webb said he believed this was the wrong approach.

“The law should change away from that idea,” he said. “We’re in this ridiculous situation whereby the goal is allowed to stand because it’s an own goal. You also get officials having to work out: was the shot on target, was it not on target? The worst-case scenario for us is that the officials decide that the ball is going wide and it’s an own goal, but then later on the goal is attributed to the player that scored, whose arm it hit. So, I think we ought to look at this and just allow the officials to determine whether it’s a normal handball offence. Did he make himself bigger? Did he deliberately handle the ball? And I don’t think [Maguire] does those things in this situation.”

Webb, who has promised greater transparency from Pro Ref, is increasingly expected to give a public verdict on controversial decisions and it was not a surprise to find Match Officials Mic’d Up scheduled for TV 48 hours after the farrago in the Manchester derby.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland celebrates after his goal in the derby was cleared to stand. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

The VAR Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus were stood down from their duties on Monday, after Pro Ref acknowledged “an error of judgment” in assessing City’s winning goal. Donohue was called on to check the decision to disallow Haaland’s 60th-minute strike for offside. Using semi-automated offside technology, Donohue was able to establish that the striker was onside and he overturned ­Oliver’s call. But he failed to spot Fernández had influenced play from an offside position, an ­infringement which Pro Ref said should have led him to recommend an on-field review.
