Webb said it was “important” this error had been acknowledged. “I was really disappointed with this outcome, we all are, none more so than the officials themselves,” he said. “They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they’re obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They’ll not be officiating again until after the international break.”

Webb said that Donohue had got “tunnel vision” while assessing the lead-up to the goal, concentrating on Haaland and not Fernández, because the on-field decision was against Haaland. “Donohue doesn’t truly evaluate the full impact of Fernández’s position,” Webb said. “He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score. He doesn’t touch the ball, but he doesn’t truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it’s down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn’t happen.”

Sports.title: Craig Bellamy says his loyalty to Wales is unquestionable after rejecting Burnley
Sports.content:
Craig Bellamy said Wales supporters should never question his commitment to the cause after he rejected the chance to manage Burnley, pointing to how he got solicitors’ letters to play for his country and refused to claim expenses on international duty.

Bellamy held talks with Burnley in the summer after the Championship club triggered a release clause in his contract but turned down the move because Wales was “the right place for me”.

He spent two years on the staff of Burnley, working as an assistant to Vincent Kompany and taking caretaker charge after the Belgian left for Bayern Munich, describing those years as “heaven”, but declined the chance to succeed Scott Parker.

His immediate focus is on Nations League matches against Portugal, Denmark and Norway, the first of which is in Lisbon a week on Thursday. Bellamy said Burnley’s interest posed a quandary but that it was ultimately a “simple” decision to stay with Wales, for whom he made 78 appearances as a forward and is under contract until the end of Euro 2028.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

While at Newcastle, Bellamy instructed independent solicitors to enable him to play after his club tried to stop him from featuring in Euro 2004 qualifiers against Italy and Finland. “The club were trying to tell me not to play: ‘[You] can’t play, we’re going to sue you if you do play,’ so I had to get independent solicitors’ letters to make sure I was able to play for Wales,” he said. “I ain’t seen ­anyone else do that.”

Bellamy said he had never submitted an expense relating to Wales duty. “Not now, not when I was a player – ever,” the 47-year-old said. “I don’t see it like that. Wales is more important, way more important to me. I charge you for me travelling here? No, I do this for free. I still do now. I’ve never put in an expense, never will.”

He also referenced his donations to Wrexham while a player. “Wrexham going out of the Football League [in 2006-07]? I donate money to Wrexham, they stay in the league,” Bellamy added. “So my commitment with Wales, I don’t believe I have to ever try and win anyone over with that. It’s there [to see], my body of work. I don’t listen to what people say. I always had that gift throughout my career. I mean it in a kind way. I had to so I could have the career I had.”

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo look reborn under Andoni Iraola - but Dominik Szoboszlai wonder strike steals the show as Liverpool pile pressure on Roberto De Zerbi
Sports.content:
It was the reaction of those not in Dominik Szoboszlai's close proximity that helped one understand the true genius behind his strike.

Defender Ronald Araujo ran to the dugouts and zipped along on the sodden turf on his knees like it was he who had scored – and done so in the World Cup final to boot.

Alexander Isak, one of the best strikers in the game, was less animated but put his hands to his head.

Awestruck, yes. Shocked, maybe not. Szoboszlai does this in training a lot and he, like his idol and predecessor to the No 8 shirt at Liverpool in Steven Gerrard, knows how to strike a ball from distance.

'It was scary, not many hit a ball like Dom,' said man-of-the-match Lewis Koumas, the academy starlet who shone.

The Hungarian chested down a loose ball, let it bounce once and unleashed a thunderous strike from 30 yards. It was an early goal-of-the-season contender and helped Liverpool progress in the Carabao Cup at the expense of a wasteful Tottenham Hotspur.

Alexis Mac Allister celebrates scoring his second goal in his last two starts for Liverpool

Cody Gakpo is flying once more after coming close to leaving Liverpool in the summer

The victory was rounded off by a goal-of-the-season contender from Dominik Szoboszlai

Szoboszlai put his finger to his ear in a gesture that might have been directed at those who gave him criticism at the weekend for a poor off-the-ball performance. Some might see him as arrogant, but if you can score goals like that, who wouldn't be?

'The goal is a worldie, outstanding,' said Iraola. 'The thing with Dom is before shooting, you trust him. With other players you might think it is too far away. With Dom, everyone is thinking he might score.'

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Mamardashvili 7.5; Frimpong 6, Araujo 6.5, Gomez 7 (Jacquet 46, 7), Kerkez 6; Nyoni 7 (Gravenberch 62, 6), Mac Allister 8; Ngumoha 7 (Barcola 72, 6), McConnell 7 (Szoboszlai 62, 6); Gakpo 7; Koumas 8 Subs not used: Alisson, Endo, Isak, Munoz, Chambers. Booked: Araujo, Frimpong, Kerkez, Iraola Scorers: Mac Allister 21, Gakpo 54, Szoboszlai 90+1 Manager: Andoni Iraola 7 TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR (4-2-3-1): Dubravka 6; Gray 6, Tosin 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 57, 6); Bentancur 6 (Fernandes 57, 6), Bergvall 6.5; Kudus 6 (Savio 75, 6), Gallagher 7 (Maddison 75, 6), Tel 5 (Solanke 85); Marmoush 5 Subs not used: Kinsky, Van Hecke, Davies, Van de Ven Booked: Marmoush, Bentancur Scorer: Gallagher 69 Manager: Roberto De Zerbi 5 Man of the Match: Koumas

The super strike ended a nail-biting finale at Anfield that saw Conor Gallagher pull a goal back, Omar Marmoush be denied by a finger-tip save and his fellow Manchester City bench-warmer Savio drag a shot wide.

Szoboszlai will take the acclaim as he often does but this victory equally belonged to his team-mates and the supporting cast after Andoni Iraola made 10 changes from the side that looked lethargic and devoid of ideas in a 0-0 weekend draw with Fulham.

The main architects of the win were two players who have points to prove at the club.

One feels unwanted amid a contract stand-off, the other the opposite after a summer departure was kiboshed – but Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo combined to lethal effect here.

First up was Mac Allister, the Argentine who last week revealed he was 'very sad' with the club for not putting a new contract on the table for him and saying they were not in a position to extend his deal at the club.

He has talked the talk but is walking the walk, this his second goal in the two starts since then after a starring role and strike against Atletico Madrid six days ago.

Sadly for the midfielder and his camp, including father Carlos, it appears Liverpool are benefiting from the uncertainty around him. He is playing with a point to prove and this frustrated version of Mac Allister is markedly better than the sloppy, lethargic version of last term.

His goal was a fine, curling finish with the inside of his foot after 21 minutes after Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha combined well and worked the ball into Mac Allister's path, via the help of an unfortunate toe from Destiny Udogie.

Then there is Gakpo. Had the summer window panned out ever so slightly differently, the Dutchman would be at Manchester City or Spurs right now, with both clubs at different times confident of signing him during a saga that felt like it was destined to end with an exit.

The pressure will pile on Roberto De Zerbi after Spurs were dumped out of the cup

Lewis Koumas, one of several youngsters trusted by Andoni Iraola in this new era, was energetic throughout

But Liverpool ultimately pulled the plug on those moves and, like his fellow goal-scorer, Gakpo is flying once more, with two goals and four assists in his first five appearances of the season.

Gakpo's strike was a thumping finish after Mac Allister's incisive assist.

Both cases should serve as a reminder to fans to not write off players so quickly. Neither were anywhere near their best last term but both have looked reborn under Iraola.

Another thing the new boss has given is a trust in youth. Koumas, 20, was the man of the match here in an outstanding display. Iraola described him as 'contagious' which is bang on: the Chester-born forward is a bundle of energy leading from the front.

Koumas spent the second half of last season on loan at Hull City and was a substitute in the play-off final. Few then could have foreseen his rise, but his hard work, attitude and pressing ability have impressed Iraola. Midfielder James McConnell is also worthy of praise.

Another deserving of a shout-out is goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili.

Despite being the first top-flight goalkeeper to concede to Tottenham this season, and being at fault for flapping at a cross in the process, it could have been more if not for two fine saves – one at the start to deny Lucas Bergvall, the other in the dying stages to thwart Marmoush.

Conor Gallagher had halved Liverpool's lead, heading home a Matheus Fernandes corner, and Anfield was soon transformed into a theatre of nerves once more but big Georgian Mamardashvili, plus Szoboszlai's wonder-strike, saw the Reds into the next round.

Roberto De Zerbi said he had won games playing much worse than tonight and he is right. But the Italian could do with a lucky break after blanking four times in the league and already being dumped out of the cup.

Spurs were better here and could have got a result on another day. De Zerbi said: 'We have to shoot more times, we have to shoot better, we have to finish better the clear situations, but we are sorry for the result, disappointed, frustrated for the result.

'I think it's unfair, but we have to accept it and to be stronger than this unlucky moment.'

Sports.title: Forget blaming JJ Gabriel - it is Man United's fault the 15-year-old wants to leave, writes OLIVER HOLT. Why would his family entrust the future of English football's hottest youth property to the greedy Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe?
Sports.content:
When a young player wants to leave a football club, it is a default mechanism in the culture of English football to blame the kid for being a prima donna with ideas above his station or, more often, point the finger at a pushy parent or an unscrupulous agent for putting dollar signs ahead of development. And so it has been with JJ Gabriel.

When the news broke on Tuesday afternoon that Gabriel, who is 15 years old and perhaps the most feted young player at Manchester United since Ryan Giggs, had asked to leave the club ahead of his 16th birthday next month, it was greeted with a mixture of dismay and horror at Old Trafford.

But instead of blaming the kid or his parents or an intermediary, or all three, the breakdown in relations between Gabriel and the club feels more like yet the latest symbol of the decline of a club that is learning the hard way that more than a decade of mismanagement at the top of the organisation comes with consequences.

At one level, that means that United can no longer attract the best players in the transfer market. This summer, Elliot Anderson, Mateus Fernandes, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Adam Wharton were said to be United's top targets in their attempts to strengthen their midfield. None of them came.

Fernandes and Tonali went to Spurs, Guimaraes went to Arsenal, Anderson went to Manchester City, Wharton stayed at Crystal Palace. United had to settle for Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, all good players but not good enough to close the gap to the teams already ahead of United.

That is the reality for United now. They are not the preferred destination for the best players in the world. Even on the back of a positive season last season when Michael Carrick and Steve Holland took the team back into the top four, United's recruitment let them down in the summer and they have started this season poorly.

Manchester United's teenage prodigy JJ Gabriel, 15, announced on Tuesday that he wants out

The breakdown in relations between Gabriel and the club feels more like yet the latest symbol of the decline of Manchester United

Who can blame him for wanting to leave the club with the way Sir Jim Ratcliffe is running it

The club is still a mess of dysfunction. The idea that they will fix the team department by department, moving on to replace a creaking defence in the next summer window, is deeply flawed. The dynamics of football teams do not work like that. It feels, once more, as if United are going backwards.

And then there is the farrago involving the club declaring war on a section of its own fans. They are trying to root out ticket touts, the club says, but the removal of hundreds of supporters' season tickets has created a poisonous atmosphere at Old Trafford at a time when Carrick least needs it.

Think about that and it feels rather amusing that some are accusing those around Gabriel of greed. Greed? United and their current clutch of misbegotten owners wrote the book on it. If there is any moral high ground in an episode like this, United will find it very hard to scramble up to it.

Switch the question around. Why would the hottest youth property in English football want to stay with the modern Manchester United? Why would JJ Gabriel's parents entrust their son to club owners like the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe? It is not surprising that the lad is looking for a way out. It would be more surprising if he wasn't.

I saw Gabriel play for United in the FA Youth Cup against Oxford United at the Kassam Stadium last February and it was obvious that all the hype about him was true. He was a special talent. It was not just that he was electric with the ball at his feet, he had an instinctive awareness of space and how to find it and vision that went beyond his years.

It is said that Carrick was planning to include him in the United squad for the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton on Wednesday evening but it may be that the club has missed a trick by not making him part of the first team at an earlier opportunity. It may be that, even at 15, Gabriel felt he was being held back.

It was expected that Gabriel was to be a part of Michael Carrick's (left) squad to face Brighton

Arsenal, for instance, handed debuts to their own prodigies, Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri, as 15-year-olds. Dowman, who has already announced himself as a spectacularly precocious talent, scored in the Premier League last season and was used in the title run-in by Mikel Arteta.

It is said that United are still hopeful they can repair the situation and retain Gabriel's services but it already feels as if it will be hard to come back from a fracture of such a public nature.

The older fans amongst us may still associate United with the Busby Babes and the Class of 92 and all the glories and the romance that came with those groups of home-grown players. But those days are long gone and the club that produced them disappeared long, long ago.

Sports.title: Nick Woltemade is ripped apart by Italian press weeks after loan move to Juventus - as £69m Newcastle flop is accused of 'doing everything WRONG'
Sports.content:
Nick Woltemade is ripped apart by Italian press weeks after loan move to Juventus - as £69m Newcastle flop is accused of 'doing everything WRONG'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Italian media have ripped into Newcastle flop Nick Woltemade despite the German striker having only just moved to Juventus.

Woltemade, 24, joined the Italian giants on a season-long loan on Deadline Day, and he has made two substitute appearances over the past few weeks.

However, after Sunday's 3-2 defeat by Sassuolo - a game in which Woltemade missed two clear-cut chances - Italian outlet Gazzetta dello Sport were heavily critical of his display.

'Woltemade is clearly having major problems integrating himself into the team's dynamic,' they wrote.

'He tried his best. But in the decisive moments, he lacks clarity in his actions, which is particularly noticeable in these games where every action can be crucial.'

They added: 'Woltemade squanders: The German lacks precision and does everything wrong.'

The Italian media have ripped into Newcastle flop and Juventus loanee Nick Woltemade

Woltemade has struggled in his two substitute appearances since joining the Italian giants

Woltemade and fellow attacker Randal Kolo Muani, who struggled on loan at Tottenham last season, have come under particularly heavy criticism after being two of the club's statement summer signings.

Writing about the pair - who are yet to 'make a difference' since joining - the same outlet said: 'Four games and not a single goal, plus several scenes that quickly circulated as mocking social media clips among rival fans.

'Clumsy ball control, botched back heel flicks that landed at the feet of the opposition, and – what is particularly troubling – hardly any dangerous scoring opportunities. No, this cannot continue. Juventus' attack is not working.'

That view was echoed elsewhere, with Corriere dello Sport similarly brutal in their assessment of the two strikers.

'How annoying is it when the very new signings you chased for months (and paid far too much for) turn out to be the biggest disappointments of the team?,' they wrote.

The latest criticism for Woltemade comes after Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti bizarrely compared him to 'a horse that likes to be petted and ridden' after his debut.

The German striker had come off the bench in the 75th minute of a clash against AC Milan, with Juventus trailing 1-0.

Woltemade nearly made an immediate impact when the ball fell kindly for him in the penalty area and he swung a boot at it, but was ultimately unable to keep his shot down as the chance went begging.

Woltemade did manage to win a free-kick in stoppage time, however, and the Turin side capitalised, with Federico Gatti heading home a dramatic equaliser to secure a valuable point against Ruben Amorim's side.

After the match, Spalletti compared his new player to a Friesian horse, the breed known for its long, flowing mane and tail.

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti previously bizarrely compared Woltemade to a Friesian horse

Spalletti told Tuttosport: 'What type of horse is he? I have a Friesian, he seems very similar to me.

'He is statuesque, he inspires a bit of fear from a physical point of view and then he is very sweet and lets himself be stroked and ridden.

'He becomes very good also in relations with his teammates. He’s good at holding his own physically, and ever since I met him, he’s been smiling constantly. He’s so happy to be here, and that’s already a big thing.'

Juventus have seven points from four Serie A games so far this season, and are back in action on Thursday when they take on NEC Nijmegen in the Europa League.

Sports.title: Moment Raheem Sterling is arrested with balloons and canisters in his £270,000 Lamborghini as he pleads GUILTY to dangerous driving and drug possession after crash while on 'hippy crack'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Raheem Sterling told police he had 'a problem' with laughing gas after submitting rush hour motorists to a terrifying 90-minutes of dangerous driving in his Lamborghini while high on the chemical.

The former England international, 31, zigzagged across the M25 and M3 motorways in his car, forcing other motorists to get out of his way, before swerving onto a slip road and crashing into a metal gate.

He was arrested by police who claim he tried to hide nitrous oxide, or laughing gas, from them by moving it to the back seat of his black Lamborghini Urus SUV, which is worth around £270,000.

Police bodycam footage shows the moment that Sterling was arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap. An officer can be heard saying 'you can put that down' to the footballer after opening his car door.

He can then be seen taking the items from his lap and putting them behind his seat.

Sterling is asked 'can you jump out for me' and who was at the wheel at the time of the crash, but does not reply.

Police bodycam footage shows the moment Raheem Sterling is arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap

Image issued by the Crown Prosecution Service shows the damage to the Lamborghini Urus being driven by Sterling

The former England international was pictured arriving in court today to face charges following a car crash in May

Sterling, 31, crashed his £270,000 Lamborghini Urus and was charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas

The officer adds: 'So you refuse to answer, okay.'

Sterling is told to get out of the car, asked his name and age at the roadside and to 'put the phone down, stop playing games. Stop tensing up.'

The former Manchester City and Chelsea star is then read his rights as he is arrested after being asked to put his arms behind his back.

His arrest, near the Minley interchange on the M3 in Hampshire, happened four weeks after he had returned to the UK following the end of an abortive attempt to revive his football career at Dutch club Feyenoord.

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen after a single vehicle collision at 8.45am on May 28. Police found six cannisters of nitrous oxide in his car.

Basingstoke Magistrates' Court heard that Sterling was so impaired by the laughing gas that he was unable to perform basic police station tests like placing his finger on his nose or placing one foot in front of another.

Barrister Simon Jones, prosecuting, said of Sterling: 'He appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting. Eye lids drooping consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.'

Motorist Fiona Jennings told police she had looked across to witness the driver of the Lamborghini with a balloon in front of his face which was so big she thought it was an air bag.

Nitrous oxide cannisters were found in the car after it was stopped by police

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen

Image shows the damage to the Lamborghini Urus which was being driven by Sterling when he was detained by police officers

It was so big that 'she had no idea how the driver would have been able to see the road ahead,' Mr Jones said. Ms Jennings described Sterling's driving as 'absolutely horrendous' and expressed 'genuine concern that the driver may kill someone.'

Evidence presented to court suggested Sterling was also inhaling laughing gas while at the wheel of the Lamborghini a full seven hours before his arrest.

A concerned witness called police after seeing the driver of the same car entering a McDonalds car park alarmingly fast at 1.10am the same morning and seeing the driver holding up 'a pink, inflated balloon.'

By 7.45am that morning, another motorist concerned by the Lamborghini erratically changing lanes, saw the driver placing a white balloon to his mouth and inhaling its contents. For 30 minutes, that motorist watched the vehicle weave from inside to outside lane and back and come close to smashing into the central reservation.

It was after Sterling had left the M3 near Farnborough, Hampshire, hit the gate and come to halt with the tyres of his wheels ripped up, that police found him sitting in T-shirt and shorts in the passenger seat of the car.

One officer told him to 'stop tensing up' after he had stepped out of the car. Sterling replied: 'I'm not tensing up.' Sterling provided breath tests, which established he was not under the influence of cannabis, cocaine or alcohol. But he later refused requests for a blood test, insisting that a lawyer of his choosing must be present, having rejected the offer of a duty solicitor. He also refused to answer any police questions.

Mr Jones said of Sterling's conduct: 'He was attempting to impose a condition on provision of a specimen. He was told the investigation could not be delayed for that reason. At the roadside, there was cooperation without the need for legal advice. When the search for the presence of drugs started, the cooperation ended.'

Sterling's barrister, Jason Bartfeld QC, told the court that there was 'extensive personal mitigation' in his case and that the footballer had taken 'voluntary steps to mitigate his difficulties.'

Mr Bartfeld agreed that this was a 'top category case' because it was a prolonged period of dangerous driving and Sterling was suffering 'serious impairment'. But he said the nitrous oxide would only have caused impairment in 'short periods' and that the chemical did not pose the same risks as cannabis or alcohol.

He claimed police had left Sterling confused about the blood sample. Sterling later told police in a statement: 'I asked for a solicitor. I did not fully understand I had not slept all night and was tired and confused.'

Sterling could face a maximum two years' imprisonment. The case was adjourned until November for pre-sentencing reports.

Sports.title: Mercurial Max Dowman makes a mockery of his opponents in Arsenal's 4-2 win at Ipswich: Star, 16, further stakes his claim for first-team place - Man United wantaway JJ Gabriel should take note, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
In the red half of Manchester, a 15-year-old child in JJ Gabriel is trying to force a way out of his club.

It's a markedly different story in the red portion of London, Max Dowman, 16, lighting up Portman Road to further bolster his case of regularly breaking into the Arsenal first team.

That is not a given, for the likes of World Cup winners Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi have yet to start in the Premier League this season, for example. Yet, Dowman is a mercurial talent, one who we'll see plenty of in the months ahead.

Having intercepted the ball in midfield, the teenager played a one-two pass with Eberechi Eze before sprightly running towards the box.

Ipswich Town's Cedric Kipre tried, and failed, to tackle the youngster while back-pedalling, before hitting the deck. Dowman reached the area before powerfully striking past goalkeeper Christian Walton on seven minutes with his weaker right foot.

The way he had embarrassed a burly 6ft 3in defender 13 years older than himself reflected what Dowman has done in his short senior career thus far: make a mockery of those much older than he.

Max Dowman (right) scored twice for Arsenal as they won 4-2 at Ipswich in the Carabao Cup

Dowman watches on as his shot flies towards the back of the goal for a fine individual opener

The 16-year-old watches on after scoring his second and the Gunners' third of the night

The attacker, playing in the No 10 role, wasn't done there. Two minutes into the second period, Zubimendi's prodded pass found the teenager into the area, who softly curled the ball home for a second goal.

Amid these strikes, he constantly looked for through balls and, in a big improvement from last season, tracked back to help his team out in defence. So, a mature performance all round.

Mikel Arteta was left purring over Dowman. He said: 'That's something very natural for him, and he can deliver those actions effortlessly. That's his biggest quality.

'He's an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play at the biggest stage and still handle the situation with such naturality.

'At 16 to already do what he does, it's just incredible.'

It was also a promising  to talented youths across the country - like Gabriel. Despite Arsenal's strength in depth as reigning Premier League champions, there is still a pathway for youngsters to breakthrough.

Dowman wasn't the only example here, Marli Salmon, 17, starting at centre back. He occasionally strayed out of position, but looked comfortable on the ball and played some solid attacking passes. He did his prospects no harm in his display, either, in a line-up involving four teenagers, including Myles Lewis-Skelly, 19, and later substitute Theo Julienne, 18.

Arteta opted to start Bukayo Saka and bring Declan Rice off the bench in the Carabao Cup third round against Port Vale last season. This time around, he had Saka on the bench and Rice at home.

Dowman's time at Arsenal contrasts with the situation of wantaway JJ Gabriel at Man United

After the insane workloads both players endured previously, Arteta seems to have learned his lesson, a positive step in the right direction.

A quirky defence featured midfielder Zubimendi at right back, while Viktor Gyokeres was given a chance up front again after starting against Napoli in the Champions League last week.

A goal up from Dowman's strike, Noni Madueke doubled Arsenal's lead after a crunching Bruno Guimaraes tackle set the ball loose.

It fell to Merino, his chip over the top reaching Madueke. He opened up his body and rifled the ball home with the outside of his left boot.

The shackled were completely off just 16 minutes in, the Gunners' players queuing to try get their names on the scoresheet.

Dowman added Arsenal's third in the second half, before Merino latched onto Zubimendi's pass - which Dowman faintly touched - and struck from outside the area, the ball cannoning in off the left post.

Anis Mehmeti pulled back a consolation goal for Ipswich, with Hale End graduate Chuba Akpom also making the scoresheet in injury time for the home side, though the night belonged to Dowman.

JJ Gabriel would be wise to take note.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parish frustrated with new boss Pierre Sage for dropping Jaydee Canvot just four games into the season
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parish is understood to have been frustrated by Pierre Sage’s choice to drop Jaydee Canvot for Saturday’s defeat by Ipswich Town.

Sage described the decision to leave the defender out of the squad as a ‘sporting’ one, following a poor display against Fulham the previous weekend and a disappointing week in training.

But Daily Mail Sport understands his stern treatment of Canvot, a young, valuable asset, has gone down badly in the boardroom.

The 20-year-old became a regular starter in the second half of last season after Marc Guehi joined Manchester City and had started Palace’s first three Premier League games under new boss Sage.

The French coach was previously praised for his hardline approach towards understudies Dwight McNeil and Evann Guessand, leaving them out against Fulham to provoke a response.

However, Canvot is viewed internally as a key part of the project and his omission has therefore been taken more negatively.

Pierre Sage leaving Jaydee Canvot out has been viewed negatively at Crystal Palace

Canvot (pictured) became a regular starter in the second half of last season after Marc Guehi joined Manchester City

Steve Parish is understood to have been frustrated by Sage’s choice to drop Canvot for Palace's defeat against Ipswich Town

Palace have suffered a disappointing start to the season, losing three of their opening four Premier League matches, including the 3-2 loss to newly-promoted Ipswich.

Sage has not yet had his best team to choose from, with Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta among those sidelined.

Their defence is unsettled, though, conceding 11 goals in their first four league games - a worse rate than Sheffield United managed during their record-breaking 2023-24 campaign, when they shipped 104 goals.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner, who won the FA Cup and Conference League while at Selhurst Park.

The Frenchman arrived from Lens, where he won the French Cup and guided the club to a second-place finish in Ligue 1.

Sports.title: Harry Brook's stunning 42-ball hundred makes you wonder what Kevin Pietersen actually has to teach him, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
On nights like this, you wonder what Kevin Pietersen might usefully teach Harry Brook.

As England's new white-ball mentor watched on admiringly from the Utilita Bowl dressing-room, their captain inspired his team to a massive 119-run win over Sri Lanka with a scintillating 42-ball century, confirming his status as the world's most exciting all-format batsman.

Pietersen would have been thrilled to have played such an innings, and not just because he never made a T20 hundred for England.

On Instagram, Ben Stokes – who had pushed for Brook to replace him as Test captain, before the job went to Joe Root – evidently agreed: 'I don't think even the genius of KP could come close to what Harry Brook has talent-wise… You are an absolute freak, Harry.'

Brook's innings contained all the daring and verve that once made Pietersen an outlier in English cricket, and plenty of the power too: after the early loss of debutant Aneurin Donald for 12, including a third-ball six, he responded by pummelling 30 off an over from the left-arm spin of Dunith Wellalage. After that, the Sri Lankans looked broken.

Brook later admitted that he had been watching highlights of Pietersen's batting during the 2005 Ashes on his phone, marvelling at the way he hit the ball to unusual parts of the ground. 'Hopefully he can have a big impact on my career,' he said. 'It's awesome to have a man of his calibre in the changing-room.'

Harry Brook hit a scintillating 42-ball century to power England to victory over Sri Lanka

On nights like this, you wonder what Kevin Pietersen might usefully teach Brook

The only pity is that Brook and Pietersen never got a chance to bat together. Instead, Brook had to make do with the companionship of Jos Buttler, who followed his 131 off 64 balls here against India in July with a brutal 80 off 44, and looked well rested thanks to a month off after the Hundred final. On another night, he would have been the headline act.

But it was Brook who stole the show in the first of six white-ball games against the Sri Lankans, having insisted to head coach Brendon McCullum that he didn't want to sit out the series and take a rare breather after the Test series against Pakistan.

That was just as well for a crowd of over 11,000 in Southampton, where in three successive T20 internationals the locals have been thoroughly spoiled, witnessing England totals of 248 for three against West Indies last summer, 257 for three against India and now 254 for four – their third-, fourth- and fifth-highest scores ever.

When Brook reached 94 off 38 balls, he had a chance to equal Phil Salt's England-record for the quickest T20 century. But he could only slice Dasun Shanaka for two to deep point, and in the end had to settle for equalling Liam Livingstone's 42-ball effort against Pakistan at Trent Bridge in 2021.

His eventual 114 off 49, with 10 fours and six sixes, meant his last three T20 innings have brought him 288 runs without being dismissed. No one would bet against him breaking Indian Tilak Varma's world-record unbeaten sequence of 336 when these teams meet in Cardiff on Thursday because no bowler right now seems capable of stopping him.

'I feel like I've let myself down a couple of times this summer,' he said. 'Thankfully I didn't give up that opportunity today. It was a special feeling to get to three figures.'

Sri Lanka will need to improve quickly if they are to have even a sniff. Faced with a mammoth target, they were three down in the six-over powerplay, with Sonny Baker taking his first white-ball international wickets, and limped to 135.

This was their 13th successive T20 defeat by England, a sequence that stretches back a dozen years and now looks in danger of extending beyond the summer. The punishment may barely have begun.

Sports.title: Dean Henderson signs new Crystal Palace contract until 2030 making him highest-paid player after summer interest from Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Dean Henderson signs new Crystal Palace contract until 2030 making him highest-paid player after summer interest from Nottingham Forest

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Crystal Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson has agreed a new contract through to 2030.

Daily Mail Sport understands that his new terms make the Palace captain their highest-paid player and add three-and-a-half years to his deal.

Former Palace manager Oliver Glasner was keen on bringing Henderson to Nottingham Forest in the summer transfer window, lodging an enquiry three days before the deadline.

But Henderson has now committed his prime years to Palace, after Daily Mail Sport revealed that contract talks were on the agenda in July.

The 29-year-old became club captain last season, leading Palace to the UEFA Conference League title. He made 52 appearances last term and kept 18 clean sheets.

He also played a crucial role in their FA Cup triumph, keeping clean sheets in the quarter-final, semi-final, and final.

Dean Henderson has played a critical role in Palace's recent success, winning the UEFA Conference League, FA Cup and Community Shield

Henderson joined Palace from Manchester United in 2023 for an initial £15million and has become a fan favourite at Selhurst Park.

The shot-stopper is currently sidelined with a foot injury, having played the first three games of the campaign while injured, but is expected to return after the international break.

Henderson won bronze with England at the FIFA World Cup, starting the third-place play-off match.

Sports.title: Liverpool beat Tottenham after stunning Dominik Szoboszlai strike - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool booked their place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup as they survived a late onslaught to beat Tottenham 3-1 and pile more misery on the visitors at Anfield.

Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo had Liverpool in complete control, before Conor Gallagher had Spurs back in the game in the latter stages. But with seconds left, Dominik Szoboszlai scored one of the goals of the season to put them out of sight.

Spurs and Liverpool both had early chances, but Lucas Bergvall was denied by Giorgi Mamardashvili, shortly before Martin Dubravka stopped Lewis Koumas’ efforts. But Mac Allister gave Dubravka no chance in the 21st minute when he fired into the top corner to open the scoring in brilliant fashion.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Roberto De Zerbi's side were made to pay the price for missed chances in the second half when Gakpo lashed in a second shortly after the break. It then looked as if it would be a procession for Liverpool, but Gallagher's header shortly before the 70th minute set up a grandstand finish.

Spurs pushed and pushed for equaliser and were only denied by a stunning Mamardashvili save as the clock ticked down. But any hopes of forcing a penalty shootout were extinguished when Szoboszlai unleashed a ferocious volley from 30 yards to settle the point.

Here are the talking points from Anfield...

‌



WALKING THE WALK

After going public with his ‘sadness’ about not being offered a new contract, Mac Allister knew his performances would immediately be under scrutiny.

Just a day after that very open press conference, the Argentine scored against Atletico Madrid. And as one of the experienced members of a much-changed XI, he provided a moment of real quality to break the deadlock.

View 5 Images Alexis Mac Allister celebrates after opening the scoring for Liverpool vs Tottenham

His season won’t be judged on performances in the early round of the Carabao Cup, but after a difficult 25/26, the early signs are that under Iraola, Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover his form.

‌



Gakpo in the groove

Make that two goals and three assists in five games this season for Gakpo. The fact that just two weeks ago, there was a chance the Dutchman was leaving Anfield now seems difficult to imagine.

Virgil van Dijk made it clear how important his compatriot was to the squad and Anfield bosses should be thanking their lucky stars a deal didn't materialise.

But if transfer speculation was needed to take his game up to the next level, then in the long term it's good news for everyone concerned. He has been one of the standout performers of the early weeks of the season.

View 5 Images Cody Gakpo scored his second goal of the season in the win over Spurs

‌



ALL CHANGE

We all know the Carabao Cup is bottom of Liverpool and Tottenham’s list of priorities this season. But that didn’t make the team selections any less disappointing.

Liverpool need to build some momentum under new boss Iraola, after winning just one of their four league games under the Spaniard. But he decided to make 10 changes to his line-up, despite having until Sunday afternoon to prepare for Bournemouth.

It was a similar story for Tottenham, who made eight changes. If Liverpool wanted to build some momentum, Tottenham just needed a result of any type. And Spurs don’t have European football to contend with.

View 5 Images Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi opted to make eight changes

‌



I’m aware this is all a bit ‘old man shouting at clouds’ and it did give a chance for some very talented youngsters to get minutes, but with a three-week international break on the way, could we have not seen slightly stronger XIs?

Had Tottenham gone stronger from the off, there's a fairly good chance they'd be in the hat for the next round.

NO ROOM FOR RICH!

While De Zerbi was happy to make a host of changes, one he wasn’t willing to make was bringing Richarlison in from the cold.

The Italian has made it clear that he will not play for the club again after turning down a new contract offer in the summer.

‌



View 5 Images Richarlison will not play for Tottenham again according to De Zerbi (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Richarlison was close to leaving in the summer, but is now set to be a glorified spectator until January.

De Zerbi stuck to his word, but there must have been a slight temptation. In six games against Liverpool as a Tottenham player, he has four goals. That kind of firepower would have been handy tonight at Anfield.

Encouraging signs

I know. Spurs fans won't want to hear this. And at the end of the day, this is another defeat - their third in six games, but in the first half particularly, there were reasons for optimism.

‌



On another day Tottenham went in at the break leading, but Bergvall and Kudus both failed to take excellent chances. Scoring a goal - their first against Premier League opposition all season is another huge positive that De Zerbi has to build on quickly.

On Saturday, they host struggling Aston Villa, where they will hope another positive performance can get their first win of the top-flight campaign.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel quit threat is a blow to Man Utd but NOT a seismic setback for Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel quit threat is a blow to Man Utd but NOT a seismic setback for Michael Carrick

The prodigiously talented 15-year-old has shocked the club by asking for his Old Trafford agreement to be cancelled but his request is not overly unusual and will happen more often

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel has asked for his Manchester United registration to be cancelled

The talk about JJ Gabriel’s prodigious talent has been loud for a long time and everything he has done in Manchester United’s youth ranks has suggested the hype could well be justified. Which is why the news he wants to leave United has caused quite a stir.

‌



For every well-publicised prodigy that actually goes on to enjoy a successful professional career at an elite level, there is a well-publicised prodigy who does not make it at an elite level. Always remember that.

‌



A scarily good 15-year-old does not necessarily turn into a scarily good 25-year-old. Freddy Adu was billed as the next Pele when playing in Major League Soccer at the age of 15. At the age of 25, he was having an unsuccessful trial at Blackpool.

‌



But in the case of Gabriel’s future, it is hard to find anyone with any serious doubt over whether he will make it or not. He is, by common consent, the brightest prospect in the land.

‌



He is an even brighter prospect, some say, than Max Dowman, who made his Premier League debut for Arsenal at 15 years and 235 days old. So, yes, it will be a blow for United if he does walk away, which certainly seems to be his intention.

The competition for marquee youngsters is intense. Rio Ngumoha was one of the most talked-about academy players in the Premier League but left Chelsea for Liverpool around his 16th birthday.

Gabriel turns 16 in three weeks’ time. Youngsters moving between powerhouse clubs is nothing new.

‌



View 3 Images JJ Gabriel was the youngest winner of the Manchester United Academy Player of the Year award (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Cesc Fabregas was a jewel of Barcelona’s fabled academy, La Masia, but walked away when he was 16 and joined Arsenal. It happens.

That is not to say Gabriel’s request will not concern United and their fans. This is Manchester United we are talking about. It should be a club that is the ultimate dream for any young player.

‌



But times have changed. For Gabriel’s generation - and probably his family’s generation - United is just another big club. They have not won a Premier League in 13 years and have not won a Champions League in 18 years.

Gabriel might look at Marcus Rashford - a predecessor as a prodigy - and wonder why the England attacker would have preferred to be at Barcelona this season. The reasons behind the decision of Gabriel and his family and his advisers are not yet crystal clear.

View 3 Images Rio Ngumoha left Chelsea for Liverpool at the age of 16 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



There is a suggestion that they thought he should be in United’s Champions League squad, in the same way Dowman was in Arsenal’s at a similar age. Whatever the reasons, they should be respected.

But it should be remembered that the old mantra about no one player being bigger than the club is still true. And especially when that player is not yet 16 years old and especially when that club is Manchester United.

Yes, it will be extremely annoying for United’s coaching staff, executives, and, indeed, fans. But of the issues Michael Carrick and the rest of those in charge of the footballing operation have, it is not a seismic setback.

Sports.title: Rugby sevens set for significant commercial boost thanks to innovative London event
Sports.content:
Rugby sevens set for significant commercial boost thanks to innovative London event

Dan James sees a unique opportunity to unite top-level rugby, businesses and new audiences under one roof when the tournament returns to the Honourable Artillery Company on Thursday

View Image James wants the event to become a significant fixture for both the sporting and business calendars and sees the collaboration as central to growing the game

The London City 7s founder believes the event can help give rugby sevens a much-needed commercial boost by bringing the sport into the heart of the City.

‌



Dan James sees a unique opportunity to unite top-level rugby, businesses and new audiences under one roof when the tournament returns to the Honourable Artillery Company on Thursday.

‌



And for James, he wants the event to become a significant fixture for both the sporting and business calendars and sees the collaboration as central to growing the game.

‌



“Rugby, and rugby sevens in particular, has always had a problem with properly commercialising itself,” he explained. “What we’re trying to do is give it a really good foundation to grow into a really serious on-pitch product.

“But for that to happen, we’ve got to connect with the London business network. We’ve got to connect with sponsors and the right partners who believe in the sport and want to be involved in it.

“For our partners like Wedlake Bell, they’re able to bring their clients and their audience, and it seamlessly integrates the business element of the event with the sporting element. And that’s key. This is just as much a business event as it is a sporting event. And we’ve packed Thursday out with some of London’s leading businesses throughout our hospitality and in our audience. So, it should be a great day.”

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Born in the heart of the Square Mile, the London City 7s launched in May 2025 with the aim of bringing world-class sevens rugby back to London after the removal of the European leg from the World SVNS Series calendar.

And once again, London City 7s, which is sponsored by Wedlake Bell, promises to bring together world-class rugby sevens teams, including the likes of two-time defending Investec Champions Cup champions Union Bordeaux-Bègles, Perpignan and the Barbarians, business networking and an unforgettable live-event experience.

‌



The inaugural event saw Harlequins edge out a Saracens side which featured England star Noah Caluori, to claim the first title in front of 3,000 corporates at the iconic HAC. With 11 teams competing across men’s and women’s competitions, the event delivers a full day of fast, high-scoring rugby, with pool stages leading through to knockout action and the finals under lights.

The day will begin with the Sport x Business Conference at 9am, before the main event kicks off when gates open at 11am, culminating in the grand finales at 8pm.

Peter Skinner, Business Development and Marketing Director at Wedlake Bell, added: “What we saw was a really great opportunity with Dan and London City 7s to bring something new to the City. It’s a fantastic, iconic venue at the HAC, but it’s also something that contributes to the players of tomorrow and the talent of tomorrow, not just today.

Article continues below

“We saw Noah Caluori burst onto the scene last year in an incredible final between Harlequins and Saracens, and it really set the scene for us.

“That’s why we’re supporting the sevens and supporting this event again after we did last year too. It dovetails really nicely with what we’re about here at Wedlake Bell in terms of excellence and quality, and particularly about talent and providing the best we can.”

Sports.title: Rangers legend Nacho Novo's son dies as he pays tribute to 'my boy'
Sports.content:
Rangers legend Nacho Novo's son dies as he pays tribute to 'my boy'

Rangers legend Nacho Novo, 47, shared on Instagram that nothing "could have prepared him" for the post to say that his "beautiful son" had died and he will be forever in "our hearts"

View 3 Images Nacho Novo said that his son had died (Image: nnovo10/Instagram)

Rangers legend Nacho Novo has said he is "absolutely broken" after the death of his "beautiful son".

‌



The former footballer, who is currently the manager of Darvel, wrote on Instagram that nothing "could have prepared him" for his son's death and payed tribute saying he will forever be in "our hearts".

‌



Heartfelt tributes have started pouring in from fellow sportspeople and fans across the world after the devastating news which he confirmed with pictures alongside his stepson Ross.

‌



The 47-year-old wrote: "Nothing in my life could’ve prepared me for this post. We are absolutely broken to share the sad news that our beautiful boy has tragically passed away. Please respect our families privacy during this extremely difficult time. Forever in our hearts my boy".

View 3 Images Novo said he was "absolutely broken" (Image: nnovo10/Instagram)

UK weather maps turn volcanic red for next 29C heatwave with 7 regions above 27C READ MORE :

Supreme Court rejects President Donald Trump’s mail ballot restrictions ahead of midterm elections READ MORE :

A Rangers FC comment said: "The thoughts of everyone at Rangers are with you at this sad time Nacho."

‌



Sports broadcaster Laura Woods wrote: "I'm so sorry for your loss Nacho, rest in peace your beautiful boy". While wrestling star Grado commented: "So sorry to hear this Nacho - absolutely heart breaking. My thoughts are with you and your family."

Gers fan page Rangers Til' I Die shared on Facebook : "Our thoughts are with Nacho Novo and his family following the heartbreaking news of the passing of his son. During this incredibly difficult time, the entire Rangers family stands behind you and your loved ones. Sending you strength and love."

Oswalds Bar, a Rangers pub in Glasgow city centre, added: "Our thoughts are with you Nacho". Ex-footballer Nazmi Albadawi scribed: "Sorry for your loss brother".

‌



Nacho, who had a heart attack in 2018, said afterwards that he called his then seven-year-old son from the operating theatre as cardiologists raced to keep him alive.

View 3 Images Novo said his son will forever be in "our hearts" (Image: nnovo10/Instagram)

He was rushed to a Berlin hospital where he underwent emergency surgery following a friendly match with Ibrox legends there. He suffered a stroke just weeks later, leaving him paralysed and unable to speak for two days. He later referred to his son as "my rock, my everything".

‌



Nacho was appointed Darvel FC manager in November last year after a stint coaching at West of Scotland Premier side Drumchapel.

The club said they were 'delighted' to appoint the former Ibrox striker who netted 47 times across 179 appearances for the light blues. In a statement last year on X: "Darvel FC are delighted to announce the appointment of Nacho Novo as the club’s new first team manager.

"Nacho brings a wealth of experience and a passion for developing talented players, and we look forward to working together as we continue to build for the future. Welcome to Darvel FC, Nacho!"

Sports.title: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola demands 'higher levels' as weekend performance called out
Sports.content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola demands 'higher levels' as weekend performance called out

Liverpool underwhelmed at the weekend as they were held to a goalless draw by Fulham with Andoni Iraola demanding considerably more come Tuesday night against Tottenham

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola was not overly impressed with Liverpool's display at the weekend

Andoni Iraola admits Liverpool should be "aiming for higher performance levels" after their lacklustre draw with Fulham at the weekend.

‌



The Reds were held to a goalless draw by the Cottagers at Anfield, Fulham's first point of the season, as they struggled to find a way through the west Londoners.

‌



It means that Liverpool are already six points off the pace set by Arsenal and Manchester City and without a win across their two Premier League games at Anfield this season. Iraola is still very much trying to get his ideas across with his tenure still in its infancy.

‌



Their Carabao Cup clash with Tottenham presents the chance for improvement, but is also their fourth game in 11 games. Iraola refused to see that as any type of excuse, insisting that will happen regularly given the amount of competitions their in, and wants to see forward strides made on Saturday's stalemate.

He said in his programme notes: "There is no point making excuses or complaining about the time that we have to recover. This kind of situation is going to happen many times this season, so we have to face it and make the best of it.

"This doesn't necessarily mean I expect us to be at our very best in every single game that we play, but we should certainly be aiming for higher performance levels than we were able to reach at the weekend and we should also be finding ways to win.

"I say this because we want to be playing in the Champions League for as long as we can this season and we also want to be in the cup competitions for as long as we can."

‌



View 2 Images The Reds couldn't find a way past Fulham at Anfield

The former Bournemouth has also hinted as changes, such is the relentlessness of the fixture list. "We have a number of players who deserve more minutes than I have been able to give them up to this point so that will come into my thinking, particularly as we also have players who have already given a lot," he said.

Liverpool's win in Europe over Atletico Madrid last week was their best result of the season so far, coming back from a goal down to beat the Spanish side. Iraola talked up the impact Anfield can have when they host Tottenham on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
