I have always written in this column that a good working relationship between top government functionaries, between ministries and their parastatals, between chief executives and their counterparts, and even between the National Assembly and agencies and industries, will generate something great for the nation. Last week, there was a demonstration of that, and what seems like a well-nurtured traction between NCC, under the Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, and the Ministry of Education, has led to something great that will positively transform young lives well beyond our time.

The idea behind the Zero Rated Access Initiative, according to the NCC Board, is to promote digital inclusion and enhance access to educational resources for students; thus prompting a valuable collaboration of the Federal Ministry of Education and other stakeholders, including the telecom operators, whose role provides the real oxygen for the entire process. One of its members, Rimini H. Makama, Executive Commissioner Stakeholder Management (ECSM), said at the launch on September 10, that the initiative is built to give every Nigerian learner a fair chance at digital education, pointing out that learning has moved online, prompting students to rely on online courses and digital libraries, among others, which all depend on connectivity that may be a scarce resource to some learners.

In her words: “The Zero-Rated Access Initiative exists to erase that line. Its principle is simple: no learner should be shut out of educational content because of where they live or what their family earns. By providing data allowances for approved educational platforms, it turns potential into opportunity, so that more young Nigerians can learn, research, build and acquire the skills a digital economy demands.” Dr Tunji Alausa, the Education Minister, who could hardly contain himself, declared excitedly, “Today’s launch represents much more than a telecommunications initiative. It is an education intervention. And most importantly, it is an investment in the future of millions of young Nigerians.”

He appealed for us to build a Nigeria where geography does not determine educational opportunity, where poverty does not prevent a child from accessing knowledge, but a country with an education system where technology becomes a great equaliser—opening doors, expanding possibilities and empowering every learner to realise his or her full potential. In simple terms, the Zero-Rated Access Initiative (ZRAI) is designed to give a data allowance of 100MB to 5 million learners or students at N100 per day. This comes to N15bn a month and totals a whopping N180bn a year for 5 million students.

This amount can give a learning average of between 2 and 5 hours daily on education websites—Reading texts/PDFs and Google searches: 5–15 MB/hour (7–20 hours); online learning platforms (mostly text): 10–25 MB/hour (4–10 hours). For some of us who could only afford education because the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo offered free education through his party, UPN, and could hardly encounter a telephone until well into the university, the launch last Thursday meant so much. It was almost very emotional as it destroyed status, class, and privileges. I have seen so many young people condemn the initiative, saying 100MB is hardly a drop in the ocean. I think this needs an explanation. The Zero Rated Access Initiative is a major corporate social responsibility (CSR) package put together by the regulator and the telecom operators for Nigerian students because of a shared concern for those who suffer digital exclusion.

The NCC Board said the Initiative will go live on October 1, 2026, and reaffirmed its commitment to monitoring its sustainable implementation. Meanwhile, the Education Minister informed that the initiative will commence with learners at the senior secondary school level and tertiary institutions and subsequently expand to other categories of learners across the country. Some operators—Karl Toriola, CEO of MTN, Dinesh Balsingh of Airtel, and Obafemi Banigbe of T2 Mobile—addressed the launch virtually and promised continuing support and sustainability of the initiative. However, it was the industry representative at the event, Engr. Gbenga Adebayo, who is the chairman of the Association of Licensed Telecom Operators of Nigeria (ALTON), who further articulated the position of his members to this writer, shortly after the launch. “For a student,” he explained, “100MB can provide meaningful daily access to learning materials, examination preparation, research and educational platforms without worrying about the cost of data. The programme currently provides 100 MB of daily access to approved platforms, including the Ministry of Education platforms and WAEC learning resources.”

Adebayo is excited about the tripartite initiative, which, he said, “is essentially a partnership around a common national objective. The Ministry identifies and provides the educational content and platforms; NCC provides the regulatory coordination and oversight; and the operators provide the network infrastructure and connectivity that allow students and educators to access the content. So, it is a good example of government and industry working together to achieve digital inclusion and improve education.” He canvassed the position of ALTON members not to allow the initiative to flag or fail, saying, “They have willingly supported the programme because we believe that investing in education is investing in Nigeria’s future. But zero-rating has a real cost to the operators—it consumes network resources and creates an open-ended financial and operational obligation if participation and usage are not properly managed.” Adebayo argued that “sustainability of the initiative should not necessarily mean that the operators want a commercial return from the students. What we need is a fair, predictable and sustainable framework—including proper beneficiary registration or opt-in, user controls, monitoring of usage and mechanisms to prevent abuse. This ensures that the benefits reach genuine students and learners while allowing operators to continue investing in the networks on which the programme depends.”

“In short, the operators are saying: we are willing to support the national education agenda, but the programme must be designed in a way that can survive and be sustained. The objective is not to withdraw the benefit; it is to make sure we can keep providing it for the long term,” as he painted a picture of hope. In the week following the furore generated by New York City’s new guidelines and restrictions, limiting student screen time and technology use in public schools, including the use of AI, starting from September 2026, a move being watched by the rest of the United States, it was interesting to see whether such fears would haunt the introduction of the Zero Rated Access Initiative.

The Education Minister seems to have addressed such fears when he declared that Zero-rating should not mean indiscriminate access to every platform that describes itself as educational. The content made available to our children must be appropriate, credible, safe, and aligned with our educational objectives and curriculum, Alausa said. However, beautiful as the initiative may look, I have my fears that it will exacerbate the digital divide immediately. Digital connectivity is poor in most rural parts of the country I have been to, and although the Board informed that infrastructure commitments by the operators are being met—8,526 out of 12,179 sites built recently to expand network coverage, capacity and quality of experience (QoE)—I am constrained to wonder whether vandalism of telecommunications infrastructure is not happening at a faster pace.

Apart from the pervasive insecurity, telecom service delivery is sabotaged, even by state agencies.

This will demand further rigorous planning by the regulator to build more alliances that can strengthen the industry and position operators to meet fresh demands from the state for its citizens. The Zero-Rated Access Initiative is a good one, but the guardrails need to be strong enough to lead to a future that looks very promising.

World.title: Gombe vows to end open defecation
World.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

The Gombe State Government has reiterated its determination to improve the water, sanitation and hygiene, WASH, sector and achieve an open-defecation-free state.

The commitment was reaffirmed as the Gombe State Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency, RUWASSA, under the Sustainable Urban and Rural Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene, SURWASH, programme, intensified sensitisation and mobilisation campaigns across Local Government Areas that have claimed Open Defecation Free, ODF, status.

The campaign commenced with a mega rally in Nafada Local Government Area, where RUWASSA engaged traditional rulers, community leaders, government officials and other stakeholders to strengthen community ownership of sanitation initiatives and sustain hygiene practices ahead of the ODF validation exercise.

The RUWASSA delegation, led by its General Manager, Engr. Mohammed Ahmed Gibrimu, FNSE, FNICE, who was represented by the Sector Lead, WASH, Yahaya Umaru, began the mobilisation at the Nafada Local Government Secretariat before proceeding to the palace of the Emir of Nafada.

Speaking at the palace, Umaru, who conveyed the General Manager’s message, commended the Emir of Nafada, HRH Alhaji Muhammadu Dadum Hamza, as well as residents and stakeholders in the LGA for their collective efforts towards improving sanitation and hygiene.

He said RUWASSA, in collaboration with the local government and other stakeholders, had continued to provide technical and institutional support towards achieving and sustaining ODF status in the area.

According to him, following Nafada LGA’s declaration of ODF status, RUWASSA had submitted the required documentation to the National Task Group on Sanitation, NTGS, for review ahead of the anticipated validation exercise.

He urged residents to sustain the momentum by maintaining proper sanitation and hygiene practices before, during and after the validation exercise.

Also speaking, the Sanitation Specialist, Alhaji Hussaini Abdulkadir, commended the people and stakeholders of Nafada for the progress recorded, stressing the need for sustained public awareness and, where necessary, effective enforcement of sanitation laws.

Earlier, in a welcome address, the Chairman of Nafada LGA, Hon. Babangida Adamu Jigawa, represented by his Deputy, Hon. Gambo Yahaya, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his continued support for the WASH sector.

He also appreciated RUWASSA for its technical support, assuring that the local government was prepared and committed to a successful ODF validation exercise.

Responding, the Emir of Nafada, HRH Alhaji Muhammadu Dadum Hamza, welcomed the RUWASSA delegation and commended the agency for prioritising Nafada in its sanitation and hygiene interventions.

The traditional ruler noted that while attaining ODF status was a significant milestone, the ultimate objective remained the protection of the health and wellbeing of residents.

He urged the people of the emirate to support and sustain the sanitation campaign, disclosing that sanctions had already been introduced against persons who violate sanitation laws.

According to him, offenders would face a fine of N10,000, in addition to community service or heavy labour.

As part of the mobilisation exercise, the Emir directed the eight district heads in the area to appear before the gathering and provide updates on the preparedness of their respective communities for the ODF validation.

Reports and testimonies presented by traditional and community leaders indicated a high level of preparedness across the LGA and reinforced the area’s readiness for the anticipated validation exercise.

The mega rally attracted government officials, WASH stakeholders, traditional and community leaders, civil society organisations, security agencies and members of the media.

The participation of the Makadan Sarki also added traditional colour to the mobilisation, which formed part of RUWASSA’s broader efforts to strengthen sanitation and hygiene practices, consolidate ODF achievements and contribute to the realisation of a cleaner, healthier and open-defecation-free Gombe State.

World.title: Dangote: Petrol cheaper in Nigeria than neighbours
World.content:
File image

ABUJA — President of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has said petrol is relatively cheaper in Nigeria than in neighbouring countries, a price difference he said has continued to encourage cross-border smuggling.

Dangote spoke in an interview with Arise Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about rising petrol prices in Nigeria.

He said the cost of petrol should be considered in relation to prices in neighbouring countries, noting that consumers in some of those countries pay between 30 and 50 per cent more.

“Expensive is relative in the sense that today, for a lot of them, there’s ignorance also. What they need to do is to ask what the neighbour’s price is,” he said.

According to Dangote, the price differential creates an incentive for traders to move petrol across Nigeria’s borders for higher returns.

“I don’t know if you know that there’s still a lot of smuggling of the same petrol we are producing to our neighbouring countries because those neighbouring countries are about 30 percent to 50 percent more expensive than Nigeria,” he said.

He cited Niger Republic as an example, saying petrol there was about 20 to 25 per cent more expensive than in Nigeria at a domestic price of N1,350 per litre.

“So what business are you going to do that will make you a 25 percent return?” he asked.

Dangote said the price difference could encourage traders to divert petrol intended for domestic markets to border communities for resale.

He also spoke about the potential impact of the ongoing crisis in the Middle East on energy supplies, saying availability could become a greater concern.

The businessman, however, assured Nigerians that the Dangote Refinery would continue supplying the domestic market.

“We will make sure that Nigeria will be fully delivered. We will deliver to Nigeria. Nigerians don’t need to worry,” he said.

“There will not be any shortage from our own part. There won’t be any shortage. There will not be any queues.

“And we’ll make sure that we keep satisfying the market.”

The comments came after petrol prices reportedly increased at some filling stations on Monday, with prices reaching about N1,400 per litre in Lagos and N1,450 per litre in Abuja.

Policy inconsistency, power supply

Dangote also identified what he described as inconsistent government policies and inadequate electricity supply as major challenges facing businesses in Nigeria.

“The greatest problem, there are two, which are still existing. One is inconsistencies in government policies. The second one is to do with lack of electricity,” he said.

He said the cost of alternative sources of energy, particularly diesel, was putting pressure on manufacturers and making production increasingly expensive.

“You cannot manufacture goods with diesel. You can see where diesel is today. You can’t even produce bread and make money today. So, we have to look at that today,” Dangote said.

The businessman also highlighted Africa’s electricity access deficit, saying about 600 million people on the continent lack access to electricity.

“We must make sure, even for us, really, as Africans, we cannot sit down and see that everybody is complaining. 600 million of our people, they actually don’t have power,” he said.

Dangote said the scale of the electricity challenge had prompted some African business leaders to consider taking direct action to help address the continent’s power deficit.

World.title: Police, experts meet on 2027 election security
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Nigeria Police Force (NPF) is set to host the sixth Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers (CARSPO 2026) in Imo State from September 21 to 24, with election security expected to feature prominently in discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The conference, themed “Developing a Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections,” is expected to bring together senior police officers, security experts, policymakers, election stakeholders and representatives of relevant institutions to review election security arrangements and identify emerging challenges.

CARSPO 2026 is being organised by the Nigeria Police Force in partnership with Lenders Consult International.

According to the organisers, discussions at the four-day conference will focus on the development of a security roadmap for the 2027 elections, with issues including election-related violence, intelligence gathering, inter-agency cooperation, deployment strategies, technology in election policing and public confidence in the electoral process.

Senior police officers from across the country, representatives of government agencies, civil society organisations, election management bodies, development partners and security experts are expected to participate.

The organisers said the conference would provide an opportunity for stakeholders to assess existing approaches to election security and consider measures for improving coordination and operational preparedness before, during and after elections.

Lenders Consult International also reaffirmed its partnership with the Nigeria Police Force, saying it had worked with the Force since 2019 on sponsorship and operational support initiatives.

Ahead of the conference, the organisers said proactive planning, training and inter-agency coordination remained important to election security, given the range of security challenges that can arise during electoral activities.

The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, is expected to lead discussions at the conference and provide strategic direction on the Force’s preparations for future electoral engagements.

Disu stressed the role of the police in maintaining security during elections.

“Stability of the electoral process largely depends on the Police as the lead agency in internal democracy,” the IGP stated.

He also emphasised the responsibility of the Force to provide a secure environment for the conduct of elections.

The organisers said recommendations from CARSPO 2026 would inform the Nigeria Police Force’s preparations and operational planning for election security ahead of the 2027 general elections.

World.title: FG Commissions KWASU ICT Centre for Youths
World.content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

The Federal Government has commissioned a TETFund/Renewed Hope Initiative-backed ICT Experience Centre at the Kwara State University (KWASU), Malete, to equip Nigerian youths with digital skills needed to thrive in a modern and competitive world.

Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, who was represented at the commissioning on Tuesday by the wife of the Vice-President, Nana Shettima, said the initiative aligned with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration, particularly its focus on youth empowerment, education, innovation and economic transformation.

She said the President was committed to creating opportunities that would equip Nigerian youths with the knowledge and skills required to compete in a rapidly changing world.

According to her, the ICT Experience Centre was a testament to the Federal Government’s commitment to advancing education, promoting digital inclusion and enhancing graduate employability.

“The TETFund/Renewed Hope Initiative ICT Experience Centre we are commissioning today represents opportunity, innovation, knowledge and the future of young people in Kwara State and beyond,” she said.

She explained that the facility was designed as a modern technology centre equipped with an ICT laboratory, interactive digital displays, conference facilities and exhibition spaces to provide an environment for learning, creativity, research and technological advancement.

KWASU is one of six tertiary institutions selected for the pilot phase of the intervention, with one institution representing each of the country’s six geopolitical zones.

Tinubu said similar centres had been commissioned at Ekiti State University on May 28, University of Cross River State on September 4 and Anambra State Polytechnic on September 10.

She added that the centres at Kaduna State University and Taraba State University would be commissioned soon.

According to her, the next phase of the intervention would cover 15 institutions in Adamawa, Bayelsa, Borno, Delta, Edo, Enugu, Imo, Katsina, Nasarawa, Niger, Ondo, Osun, Rivers, Yobe and Zamfara states, where construction is ongoing.

She said the expansion demonstrated the administration’s commitment to ensuring that more Nigerian youths, regardless of their locations, had access to digital learning opportunities.

Tinubu urged students to take ownership of the facility, maximise the opportunities it provides and use technology positively to improve their lives, communities and the nation.

Earlier, Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq said his administration’s vision was to ensure that every young person in the state acquired the skills and opportunities needed to succeed in a changing world.

He urged the university management to make judicious use of the facility, saying it should support students and help generate innovations, businesses, jobs and sustainable solutions to challenges facing communities.

“Technology and digital skills now shape how we learn, work and create opportunities. Our young people must, therefore, have access to the skills and techniques they need to compete anywhere in Nigeria and across the world,” AbdulRazaq said.

The governor said his administration would continue to invest in education and human capital development.

He noted that the state had expanded KWASU into a multi-campus institution, with the completion of its Osi and Ilesha Baruba campuses, while plans were underway for another campus in Ajase-Ipo.

Also speaking, the Executive Secretary of TETFund, Architect Sonny Echono, said the centres were being established across selected universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, with KWASU hosting the facility for the North-Central zone.

He said the initiative was designed to enhance graduate employability, foster innovation and position Nigeria to participate more effectively in the global technology-driven economy through practical training and digital skills acquisition.

Echono said the ICT Experience Centre would equip students and lecturers with critical digital skills in areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics and software development.

“The centre being commissioned today is one of the foremost ICT Experience Centres being delivered across the country, and the third to be commissioned this year,” he said.

He added that the facility was equipped with modern digital devices, computer systems and relevant software to facilitate training, practical learning and skills development.

The centre, according to him, was also furnished and fully air-conditioned, with supporting power and municipal infrastructure.

The Vice-Chancellor of KWASU, Prof. Shaykh-Luqman Jimoh, described the facility as an investment in human capital, innovation, entrepreneurship and the future of Nigeria.

He said the centre would provide students with opportunities to develop practical digital skills and engage with contemporary technologies, while also serving as a hub for interdisciplinary engagement.

“The centre represents vision, belief and an investment in the Nigerian youth to better shape the future of our nation,” Jimoh said.

World.title: Higher SSB Tax may raise prices – Report warns
World.content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, ABUJA

A new report by ThinkBusiness Africa has warned that the proposed increase in Nigeria’s excise duty on sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs) could significantly raise prices of soft drinks, while its impact on obesity, diabetes and hypertension remains uncertain.

The report examined the proposed amendment to the Customs, Excise Tariff, Etc. (Consolidation) Act (CETA), which seeks to replace the existing N10-per-litre excise duty with an ad valorem tax.

According to the report, the proposed system could raise the effective tax burden to about N130 per litre based on prevailing beverage prices.

It said the change would make taxation dependent on the value of beverages rather than the volume produced, potentially increasing prices and placing additional administrative pressure on manufacturers.

Citing modelling by the Centre for the Study of the Economies of Africa (CSEA), as referenced in a submission by the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, ThinkBusiness Africa said a N130-per-litre tax could result in a 39 per cent increase in retail prices and a 29 per cent reduction in annual per capita consumption of SSBs.

It also projected that annual industry output could decline from N1.5 trillion to N1.1 trillion by 2030, while the production index could fall from 78 to about 40.

The report, however, stressed that the figures were modelled scenarios and did not represent observed outcomes.

On the public health implications, ThinkBusiness Africa acknowledged evidence that taxes on SSBs could reduce purchases of taxed beverages, but said evidence was less conclusive on whether such reductions would translate into lower rates of obesity, diabetes and hypertension.

“Chronic diseases are influenced by several factors, including overall diet, physical activity, income, education and access to healthcare,” the report said.

It also questioned the proposed use of beverage value as the basis for the tax, arguing that a levy directly linked to sugar content could better achieve the health objective.

The report cited South Africa and the United Kingdom, where sugar-related taxes are linked to sugar content or specified thresholds, saying such systems could encourage manufacturers to reformulate products and reduce sugar levels.

ThinkBusiness Africa said more than 133 million Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty, with households already facing weak purchasing power and rising living costs.

“For many households, the immediate effect of a higher SSB tax will be straightforward: higher prices.

“For manufacturers, distributors and retailers, the consequences may include higher costs, weaker demand and pressure on production. This matters because the beverage sector is not an isolated industry. It is connected to agriculture, sugar supply, packaging, logistics, transportation, wholesale and retail,” it said.

The report also cited data from the National Sugar Development Council showing that total sugar consumption fell from about 1.72 million tonnes in 2022 to 1.44 million tonnes in 2023, while domestic production dropped from 46,479 tonnes to 30,053 tonnes.

Although the declines could not be attributed solely to the existing SSB tax, the report said they reflected a difficult operating environment characterised by inflation, exchange-rate pressures, rising input costs and weaker consumer demand.

It further warned that a higher tax would not necessarily guarantee increased or sustainable government revenue, as reduced consumption, lower formal-sector production and a shift to informal markets could shrink the taxable base.

ThinkBusiness Africa therefore called for a comprehensive assessment of the proposed tax, greater transparency on revenue generated from the existing N10-per-litre levy and consideration of a sugar-content-based tax.

It also recommended stronger non-tax measures, including public health campaigns, promotion of physical activity, early screening for diabetes and hypertension, and improved primary healthcare.

The report said Nigeria needed stronger measures to tackle diabetes, obesity and hypertension, but cautioned that a substantially higher SSB tax should not automatically be equated with an effective public health policy.

World.title: Kebbe Council assists 150 households displaced by banditry
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — Kebbe Local Government Area of Sokoto State has distributed food items and cash assistance to 150 households displaced by bandit attacks across several communities.

The intervention, supervised by the council chairman, Hon. Musa Garba Kuchi, was carried out on Monday at the palace of the District Head of Kebbe, Sarkin Kabbin Kebbe, Hon. Lawal Labbo Margai, in Kebbe town.

Kuchi said the beneficiaries were drawn from communities affected by bandit attacks, including Ungushi, Girkau, Margai, Kebbe East and Kebbe West.

He said the beneficiaries were residents who had been forced to abandon their homes and livelihoods because of insecurity and were currently taking refuge in Kebbe town.

“The beneficiaries are people who have been forced to abandon their homes and livelihoods because of insecurity and are currently taking refuge in Kebbe town,” he said.

Kuchi said the intervention was intended to cushion the hardship faced by displaced households, adding that the council would continue to support residents affected by insecurity.

“The council remains committed to standing with our people in these difficult times. This support may be little, but it is our way of showing that you are not forgotten,” he said.

The chairman commended Sokoto State Governor Ahmed Aliyu for what he described as sustained efforts to strengthen security and protect communities affected by banditry.

He said investments in security, including the provision of combat vehicles and other equipment to security agencies, had boosted the operational capacity of personnel deployed to affected areas.

“Government’s investment in security is already yielding positive results. Our troops are taking the fight to the bandits in their hideouts, and this has given some of our communities the confidence to begin returning to their homes,” Kuchi said.

He called for continued support for security agencies, stressing that tackling banditry required collaboration among government authorities, security agencies, traditional institutions and communities.

Kuchi pledged that the council would sustain humanitarian assistance to victims of insecurity until displaced residents could safely return to their communities and rebuild their livelihoods.

He also called for stronger collaboration among the federal, state and local governments to address the causes and consequences of banditry.

The chairman urged religious leaders and residents to intensify prayers and support peace-building efforts, saying lasting security was essential for the restoration of economic activities and development in Kebbe and the wider state.

In his remarks, the District Head of Kebbe, Hon. Lawal Labbo Margai, commended the council and state government for responding to the plight of residents displaced by insecurity.

“We appreciate the concern demonstrated by the local government and the state government towards our people who have been compelled by insecurity to abandon their communities,” Margai said.

The traditional ruler, a former Speaker of the Sokoto State House of Assembly, urged those handling the distribution to ensure that the relief materials and financial assistance reached genuine beneficiaries.

“Let the relief materials and financial assistance reach the genuine beneficiaries. There must be fairness, justice and transparency in the distribution so that no vulnerable household is deprived of what has been provided for them,” he said.

Margai also prayed for the success of ongoing security operations and expressed hope that affected communities would regain sufficient security for displaced residents to return home.

The exercise was witnessed by the Secretary of Kebbe Local Government, Alhaji Shamsudeen Umar Mai’akwai, councillors, including Hon. S.A. Maitunbi, imams, traditional title holders and community leaders.

World.title: Ebonyi PDP women decry hardship, back Odii
World.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Women Leader in Ebonyi State, Mrs Chinyere Nwele, has criticised the administration of Governor Francis Nwifuru, alleging hardship, neglect and unfulfilled promises under the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) government.

Nwele spoke during a meeting with women from Umu Ekumaenyi in Ezza land, where she assessed the performance of the state government and declared support for the PDP governorship candidate, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, ahead of the 2027 election.

She said the women had expressed concerns over what they described as a sense of neglect and exclusion from the affairs of the state.

Nwele alleged that the APC administration lacked clear direction and had failed to meet the expectations of residents in key areas of governance.

“When a square peg is forced into a round hole, there is bound to be heavy failure of the entire system,” she said.

The PDP leader also alleged that despite receiving substantial monthly allocations, the state government had not done enough in human capital development, education, infrastructure and healthcare.

She, however, presented Odii, popularly known as Anyichucks, as an alternative, describing him as a candidate with the vision, capacity, exposure and business experience to reposition the state.

According to Nwele, an Odii administration would prioritise road construction, healthcare, rehabilitation of infrastructure, innovation and human capital development, while empowering farmers and creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive.

She expressed confidence that the proposed changes would become reality if Odii is elected governor in February 2027.

Nwele also urged the women to remain focused on the 2027 election, arguing that good governance should be measured by development and service delivery rather than threats or intimidation.

“Ebonyi is now wiser,” she declared.

The meeting ended with the women of Umu Ekumaenyi expressing readiness to mobilise support for the PDP ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

World.title: Insurer Unveils Short-term for Businesses and Visitors
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

Leadway Assurance, a member of Leadway group has unveiled a short-term insurance product to attend to the need of travellerduring the festive periods.

The product targeted to diaspora Nigerians visiting their home country during the Yuletide was lunched in Lagos recently bringing together key stakeholders from across the travel, lifestyle, tourism, aviation, media and financial services sectors.

At the lunch, Leadway Executive Director Retail & Partnership, Kikelomo Fischer, highlighted the growing need for flexible insurance solutions tailored to diaspora Nigerians, business travellers, tourists, students and other short-term visitors, as well as the businesses that serve them during their stay in the country.

She said the Leadway Arrival Pack was developed as a seasonal insurance solution for periods when travel, gatherings and commercial activity naturally increase.

“It is designed to give visitors and participating businesses greater confidence and peace of mind by providing protection against unexpected disruptions and risks that may arise during short-term stays in Nigeria” .

According to her traditional insurance plans are often structured around longer-term coverage, leaving individuals on brief visits with limited options for protection.

She noted that with increasing international travel, diaspora homecomings, business visits and tourism activity, the need for flexible, temporary insurance solutions has become increasingly important.

She said Leadway Assurance was addressing the gap through the Arrival Pack, offering accessible short-term coverage tailored to the realities of temporary stays.

World.title: Asunmo Emerges CeBIH Chairman, Pledges Support for PSV
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

Group Head, e-Business and Transaction Banking, Premium Trust Bank, Mrs. Abidemi Asunmo, has emerged as the 10th Chairman of the Committee of e-Business Industry Heads (CeBIH), pledging to support the implementation of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) Payment System Vision 2028 (PSV 2028), strengthen industry advocacy and promote digital identity across Nigeria’s financial ecosystem.

Asunmo, unveiled an agenda centred on Payment System Vision 2028 implementation, advocacy, combat against fraud, digital identity, ethical use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and inclusion during the 2026 CeBIH election and swearing-in ceremony.

Unveiling the administration’s priorities I a statement, Asunmo said: “At the top of our agenda is our commitment to supporting the successful implementation of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Payment System Vision 2028,” which she said provides a roadmap covering “financial inclusion, digital payments growth, open banking, cybersecurity and regulatory efficiency.”

She pledged that CeBIH would strengthen engagement with regulators and stakeholders to ensure that the vision translates “from policy into meaningful industry outcomes.”

On advocacy and inclusion, Asunmo said CeBIH would expand its engagement beyond regulators and industry stakeholders to ordinary Nigerians and consumers of banking services.

“Our advocacy cannot stop with regulators and industry stakeholders; we must increasingly engage the Nigerian public—the ultimate beneficiaries of the financial ecosystem we are helping to build,” she said.

World.title: NAICOM Debunks N100bn Recapitalisation Fraud Claim
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

The National Insurance Commission (NAICOM), has debunked recent publication on N100 billion fraudulent insurance recapitalisation and allegations on detention of its director and commissioner for insurance, Mr Olusegun Ayo Omosehin, saying the publication was false, misleading, malicious and deliberate misrepresentation of facts.

The commission said the publication on September 9th, 2026 by promoters of NICON Insurance and Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation both of which were under liquidation was deliberately designed to misinform the public, undermine regulatory processes, and cast aspersions on the integrity of the Commission and its officials.

“The attention of the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) has been drawn to a publication titled “100 billion fraudulent insurance recapitalisation: EFCC detains NAICOM director and commissioner, both on bail”, published on 9 September 2026 being sponsored by the promoters of NICON Insurance Plc and Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation, both of which are currently under liquidation”.

World.title: Subscription to FG Bond Crosses N13tn as Rate on 10-Year Hits 16.79%
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Despite modest yields, total subscription to FGN Bond between January to September 2026 crossed historic high of N13 trillion to N13.72 trillion.

The high demand for the FGN Bond is on the backdrop of large institutional investors demand, relatively attractive rates that encouraged pension funds, banks, insurance companies among others to lock in returns.

FGN Bond auction during the period under review is on the back of sustained government reliance on the domestic debt market to fund fiscal obligations amid constrained external financing conditions.

According to the FGN bond auction result obtained by THISDAY, the government through the Debt Management Office (DMO) in the nine months of 2026 offered to raise N8.35 trillion to bridge budget deficit.

The debt office, according to its monthly FGN auction results, however, raised an estimated N7.14 trillion during the nine months period.

Investor participation was broad-based, but demand was heavily skewed toward the long end of the curve, reflecting continued preference for higher yields in a tight monetary environment.

However, the latest auction results show strong but selective demand across the two instruments, with the 12-year paper dominating subscriptions.

This week, the DMO in its September 2026 FGN bond auction, issued 16.79% FGN SEP 2036 (New Issue) and 15.45% FGN JUN 2038 (Re-opening), offering a total of N1 trillion.

Total demand settled at N1.49 trillion, with the DMO eventually allotting N748.64 billion. The stop rate on the FGN SEP 2036 and FGN JUN 2038, which were on-the-run last month, expanded to 16.7900% and 16.8500%, respectively.

DMO data showed that investor demand was strongest at the long end, while shorter tenors saw relatively softer participation, particularly the 10-year bond which was over-subscribed.

The amount offered by DMO fell from N1.10 trillion in August to N1 trillion in September 2026, a reduction of N100 billion or 9.1per cent. This indicates a slightly tighter FGN Bond supply in September 2026.

Reducing the amount of securities available can potentially help the FG manage debt. Subscriptions fell from N1.727 trillion in August 2026 to N1.495 trillion in September 2026, representing a much larger 13.5per cent decline.

Despite this decline, demand remained strong: investors still subscribed to about 1.49 times the amount offered in September 2026.

In addition, the amount allotted declined from N805.16 billion to N748.64 billion, a decrease of only seven per cent.

Consequently, the proportion of the amount offered that was allotted increased from 73.2 per cent in August to 74.9 per cent in September. In August, the coverage ratio was higher at 1.57 times. So, while demand weakened, the auction remained oversubscribed.

The DMO had targeted N1 trillion from the domestic debt market in its September 14 FGN bond auction, with a new 10-year issue and a reopening of an existing bond.

According to the DMO’s auction circular, the offer comprises N400 billion of the new FGN September 2036 bond and N600 billion of the 15.45% FGN June 2038 bond, which is being reopened.

Analysts attributed the strong demand for FGN bonds to modest yields, stressing that the over-subscription also showed investors’ confidence in the federal government’s ability to meet its debt obligations.

World.title: FG Kicks off  Payment of Additional Exit Benefits Scheme to Retirees
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

The federal government has commenced payment of Additional Exit Benefits to retirees of Treasury Funded Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs).

This was disclosed by the National Pension Commission (PenCom) in a statement to the media.

The commission said so far government had paid approximately N1.1 billion to 175 retirees who exited the Federal Public Service between 1 January and 31 August 2026.

PenCom said the payment was being made under the Federal Government Exit Benefit Scheme (EBS), approved by the Federal Executive Council and effective from 1 January 2026.

According to the commission, the scheme provides an additional financial benefit to Federal Government employees at retirement, alongside their pension benefits under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS).

“Under the Scheme, Federal Civil Servants who have served for at least 10 years are entitled to an Exit Benefit equivalent to 100 per cent of their total annual emolument.The commencement of payment marks yet another watershed moment for the CPS as efforts are intensified at delivering more benefits to retirees beyond what they have accumulated in their Retirement Savings Accounts during their service period,”it said.

PenCom further said it was noteworthy that the federal government had led the way in offering additional benefits to its retirees, which was worthy of replication by other employers.

According to the commission, to ensure the smooth implementation of the Additional Exit Benefits Scheme, the 2026 Appropriation provided the sum of N32.90 billion. So far, the Federal Government has released N12.3 billion into the dedicated Exit Benefit Scheme Account maintained with the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN).

PenCom said it was supporting the implementation of the scheme by working with the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF), the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (OAGF), Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) and other stakeholders to facilitate the processing and payment of the benefits.

World.title: Financial Markets Dealers: N3.56tn Liquidity Inflow Expected This Week
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

the Financial Markets Dealers Association (FMDA) has stated that an estimated N3.56 trillion is expected to flow into Nigeria’s financial system this week, up from N3.02 trillion projected in the previous week.

The projected inflow represents 18 per cent week-on-week increase, with Open Market Operations (OMO) maturities accounting for the bulk of the expected funds.

The FMDA, in its Weekly Market Snapshot stated: “Looking ahead, an estimated N3.56 trillion is expected to flow into the financial system this week, with OMO maturities accounting for about 86 per cent of projected inflows.”

OMO maturities, FMDA said are expected to provide N3.06 trillion, compared with N2.94 trillion last week, while Treasury Bills maturities are projected at N449.76 billion, significantly higher than the N71.37 billion recorded in the previous week.

“Other inflows include N39.65 billion from FGN bond coupons, N5.87 billion from corporate bond coupons and N8.47 billion from commercial paper maturities. However, the expected inflow comes amid tighter liquidity conditions, with system liquidity falling 47.12 per cent week-on-week to N2.46 trillion, from N4.67 trillion,”it said.

The FMDA attributed the decline to the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) liquidity management operations, noting that the apex bank “sterilised approximately N5.46 trillion via OMO and NTB auctions.

Meanwhile, the naira remained resilient, with the NFEM rate averaging N1,324.95/$, while the parallel-market rate averaged N1,394.40/$.

The FMDA also noted that average Brent crude rose 8.06 per cent to $101.67 per barrel, while external reserves increased 0.52 per cent to $54.41 billion.

World.title: NFEM FX Turnover Hits $1.45bn in One Day, Weekly Volume Jumps 47%
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

Trading activity on Nigeria’s official foreign exchange market surged last week, with daily turnover climbing to a record $1.45 billion as the market recorded one of its busiest trading sessions since the beginning of the available data series.

Data from the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) showed that turnover rose to $1.454 billion on September 10 from $544.11 million the previous day, representing a 167.2 per cent increase within a single trading session.

The figure was also more than double the $674.38 million recorded on Thursday, September 3, in the preceding week, representing a 115.6 per cent week-on-week increase in turnover for the corresponding trading day.

The September 10 turnover was the third-highest single-day turnover recorded in the NFEM data, which covers transactions from December 2024 to date.

It came behind the $1.82 billion recorded on May 12 and $1.53 billion on July 21.

The sharp increase on Thursday was accompanied by 470 deals, the highest number of daily deals recorded during the week. Interbank transactions accounted for $357.30 million of the day’s total turnover.

The spike on September 10 helped lift total NFEM turnover for the five trading days ended September 11 to $3.87 billion, representing a substantial 47.2 per cent increase from the $2.63 billion recorded in the preceding week.

Despite the surge in value traded, the number of transactions was relatively stable, with 1,572 deals recorded during the week, compared with 1,580 deals in the previous week, a marginal decline of 0.5 per cent.

The figures suggest that the sharp increase in turnover was driven more by the size and value of transactions than by a corresponding increase in the number of deals.

Trading activity during the week started at $482.24 million on Monday, September 7, before rising sharply to $933.78 million on Tuesday.

Turnover moderated to $544.11 million on Wednesday before the major spike to $1.45 billion on Thursday. Activity subsequently eased to $458.99 million on Friday.

The Tuesday figure was also significantly higher than the $574.42 million recorded on the corresponding Tuesday of the previous week, while Wednesday’s $544.11 million was below the $658.46 million recorded on September 2.

Friday turnover of $458.99 million was also lower than the $495.70 million recorded on September 4.

The week-on-week increase was therefore concentrated around the sharp expansion in trading on Tuesday and, particularly, Thursday.

The weekly performance also placed September 7–11 among the busiest trading weeks in the NFEM since the beginning of the available series.

However, it did not set a weekly record. The highest weekly turnover recorded in the dataset was $5.28 billion between August 17 and 21, followed by $4.82 billion between July 20 and 24 and $3.97 billion between March 9 and 13.

The latest $3.87 billion therefore ranks as the fourth-highest weekly turnover in the available NFEM data.

The performance is nevertheless notable because the market achieved the volume despite recording fewer deals than in some of the earlier high-turnover weeks.

For instance, the July 20–24 week generated $4.82 billion from 1,610 deals, while the August 17–21 week recorded $5.28 billion from 1,420 deals.

By comparison, the September 7–11 week generated $3.87 billion from 1,572 deals.

Interbank activity also contributed significantly to the week’s performance. Total interbank turnover stood at approximately $763.24 million during the five-day period, with Thursday alone accounting for $357.30 million.

World.title: Nigeria: Global Recognition Signals Investor Confidence
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

writes on the growing international recognition of Nigeria’s economic reforms, as the country records a string of positive signals from global financial institutions, investors and rating agencies, raising hopes that the difficult policy adjustments of the past three years are beginning to translate into stronger investor confidence

For an economy that spent years struggling to convince investors that it could provide a predictable environment for capital, Nigeria is beginning to receive an unusual form of validation: the outside world is starting to change its assessment. The evidence is coming from different directions.

For instance, FTSE Russell recently announced that it is restoring Nigeria to its Frontier Market classification after the country was pushed into “Unclassified” status in 2023 over concerns about foreign exchange liquidity and investors’ ability to repatriate capital.

Also, J.P. Morgan has admitted Nigerian government bonds into its new Government Bond Index–Emerging Markets Edge, potentially opening the door to billions of dollars in benchmark-linked investment.

Earlier this year, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) removed Nigeria from its grey list after the country addressed deficiencies in its anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing framework.

The European Union subsequently removed Nigeria from its list of high-risk third countries for money laundering and terrorist financing.

The three major international rating agencies Fitch, Moody’s and S&P have also moved in a more favourable direction, with S&P upgrading Nigeria to B, Fitch affirming its B rating with a stable outlook and Moody’s revising its outlook to positive.

Then there is the more mundane but perhaps more telling evidence: foreign exchange is becoming easier to access, Nigerian naira cards are working abroad again, banks are raising international spending limits, reserves have climbed above $54 billion and diaspora remittances are approaching the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) $1 billion monthly target.

Taken together, these developments suggest something bigger than a collection of isolated policy announcements. They suggest that Nigeria’s economic reforms are beginning to produce the one outcome that policymakers have been seeking since 2023, confidence.

Reform Architecture

One distinguishing feature of the Bola Tinubu administration’s economic programme is that the key policymakers arrived with a clear diagnosis of the country’s problems.

The reforms were painful because they targeted some of the most entrenched distortions in the economy: fuel subsidy, multiple exchange rates, monetary financing of fiscal deficits, weak public finances and undercapitalised banks.

Government sources volunteered that the objective was not simply to make Nigeria look better to international investors. “It was to make the economy function differently. That distinction is important,” said a government official who do not want his name in print.

Recently, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its 2026 Article IV assessment, said sustained reforms since 2023 including ending fuel subsidies and deficit monetisation, tightening monetary policy and liberalising the exchange rate had strengthened macro-economic stability, rebuilt external buffers and improved foreign exchange market functioning. It also noted that portfolio inflows had resumed and Nigeria had regained access to international markets.

Former Finance Minister Wale Edun was similarly emphatic when he represented Nigeria at the IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings.

“The overall message from the Spring Meetings is encouraging. Nigeria’s global economic standing is improving. Our reform story is being taken seriously and indeed used as an example. Our resilience is better understood, and our investment case is strengthened, with confidence returning at a faster pace,” Edun said.

CBN Monetary Reset

At the centre of the adjustment has been the CBN’s return to orthodox monetary policy. The CBN under the leadership of Olayemi Cardoso inherited an economy in which foreign exchange shortages, multiple exchange rates, monetary financing and weak confidence had become mutually reinforcing.

The response was to allow the FX market to become more market-driven, tighten monetary conditions, improve transparency and rebuild the central bank’s credibility.

The process was expensive. Interest rates rose sharply and the naira initially weakened substantially. But the CBN’s argument was that restoring price and currency stability required breaking with the previous policy framework.

Cardoso has consistently linked the monetary reforms to investor confidence.

Speaking recently, he pointed to the change in Nigeria’s external position as evidence of the progress made.

“Anybody that wants to argue about what the impact of these reforms have been, go and look at the results,” he said, pointing to the dramatic improvement in reserves and the strengthening of the external buffer.

He added that reserves had reached around 10 months of import cover, noting that these were precisely the indicators international investors examined before taking positions in a currency.

“Doing this consistently is what is giving confidence to not just internal stakeholders, but those who also operate internationally,” Cardoso said.

The governor’s point is increasingly visible in the FX market.

The reforms have not eliminated volatility, but they have substantially reduced the distortion between official and parallel markets. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of Economy, Dr Taiwo Oyedele recently noted that the premium, which had once exceeded 60 per cent, was now below five per cent.

Return of the Dollar

Perhaps the most practical evidence of the reform dividend is that foreign exchange is becoming less difficult to obtain.

For years, the problem was not merely that the naira was weak. It was that dollars were frequently unavailable through official channels.

That affected businesses, airlines, foreign investors and ordinary Nigerians travelling or paying for services overseas.

The improvement in liquidity is now being felt by consumers.

Nigerian banks have expanded international transactions on naira cards, while some have raised spending limits. Cardoso recently offered a remarkably simple description of the change.

Cardoso while speaking at the BusinessDay CEO Forum recently said: “When you travel today, you go with your naira card. It works. It has brought back the way the outside world looks at us. In the past, you go there, the card doesn’t work. Can’t pay for your goods. They look at your naira card. They throw it back at you. Not any longer.”

For the ordinary Nigerian, that may appear like a banking convenience. For investors, it is evidence that the country’s foreign exchange and payment infrastructure is functioning more normally.

Reserves, Remittances and External Buffer

The stronger FX market has coincided with a dramatic improvement in reserves.

Nigeria’s gross external reserves reached $54.48 billion on the 11th of September, up more than $12 billion from a year earlier.

Cardoso has also pointed to the changing structure of FX inflows, particularly diaspora remittances.

The CBN governor has repeatedly said Nigeria was targeting monthly remittance inflows of $1 billion, noting that the country had already made significant progress towards that goal with July recording $947 million inflow. The significance is larger than the dollars themselves.

Nigeria is gradually replacing an environment where foreign currency was scarce and heavily rationed with one where inflows are increasingly being captured through formal channels. That again is precisely the kind of market infrastructure investors want to see.

Most Underrated Reform

Meanwhile, market watchers stressed that if FTSE Russell and J.P. Morgan represent recognition from the capital markets, Nigeria’s exit from the FATF grey list represents recognition from the global financial system.

Nigeria was removed from the FATF list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring in October 2025 after demonstrating progress on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing reforms. FATF specifically cited improvements in risk assessment, financial-sector supervision, beneficial ownership information, financial intelligence, investigations and prosecutions.

The significance is considerable. Cardoso said Nigeria’s grey-listing had potentially cost the economy more than $30 billion in capital inflows, based on the historical impact of grey-listing on capital flows.

“Exiting the list therefore signals a major restoration of confidence and eases compliance frictions for correspondent banks,” he said.

The subsequent removal from the EU’s high-risk AML/CFT list reinforced that message.

For banks and international investors, analysts believe lower compliance friction means lower transaction costs and fewer obstacles to cross-border financial activity. It is therefore another piece of the investor-confidence puzzle.

Reopening the Door

The changing view of Nigeria is perhaps most obvious in the capital market. Nigeria’s return to the FTSE Russell Frontier Market Index, effective September 21, reverses its 2023 exit, which was largely linked to challenges around FX liquidity and investors’ ability to move their money out of the country.

Commenting on the development, Oyedele said the return was about more than just being back on the index. J.P. Morgan’s latest decision strengthens the case.

Nigeria has been assigned a 7.40 per cent weighting in the new GBI-EM Edge index, translating to roughly $17.47 billion of eligible Nigerian government debt.

Oyedele described the inclusion as “a clear, independent endorsement” of the reform agenda and said it reflected the confidence international capital markets now place in Nigeria’s economic management.

The $17.5 billion is not guaranteed new investment. Rather, it represents the eligible Nigerian debt corresponding to the country’s index weighting, with benchmark-tracking funds expected to adjust their portfolios over time.

But even that potential matters. It means Nigeria is once again positioning itself to benefit from institutional capital that was previously constrained by market-access concerns.

Oyedele, was also quoted to have said the inclusion was an independent validation of Nigeria’s ongoing economic reforms.

Oyedele stated, “This inclusion is a clear, independent endorsement of the discipline behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s reform agenda. It reflects the confidence international capital markets now place in Nigeria’s economic management, and it lowers the cost of financing our development priorities. We remain focused on the work still required to earn full reinstatement in JP Morgan’s flagship index.”

Rebuilding Banking System

The reform story is not confined to FX and capital markets.

The banking sector recapitalisation programme has also delivered a significant result. 33 of Nigeria’s 37 banks had met the new capital requirements, raising approximately N4.65 trillion in fresh capital.

For Cardoso, whose monetary-policy agenda depends heavily on a stable financial system, stronger bank balance sheets are essential. Analysts agree that a better-capitalised banking system is more capable of absorbing shocks, supporting credit growth and financing the investment cycle that policymakers ultimately want to create.

Ratings Agencies Take Note

The changing perception is also reflected in Nigeria’s sovereign ratings. S&P upgraded Nigeria to B from B- in May, while Fitch retained its B rating with a stable outlook and Moody’s revised its outlook to positive from stable, citing stronger reserves and improved economic resilience.

While the challenges remain, the direction is clear: Nigeria’s credit story is improving. Even S&P Global’s decision to acquire a majority stake in Agusto & Co. adds to the growing international interest in Nigeria’s financial markets.

Hard Part Begins

There is, however, an important caveat. Investor confidence is not the same thing as household prosperity.

Nigeria still faces high living costs, inflationary pressures, elevated interest rates, weak purchasing power and deep structural challenges. The administration itself acknowledges that macroeconomic stability is only the first stage.

Oyedele recently said the government’s next challenge was to translate the gains from stabilisation into shared prosperity.

That is the test that will determine whether the reform programme becomes a lasting economic transformation rather than simply a successful stabilisation exercise.

For now, though, the evidence is increasingly compelling.

The FATF grey-list exit shows that Nigeria’s financial system is becoming more trusted. The EU delisting shows that the improvement is recognised beyond the African financial system.

FTSE’s return shows that international equity investors can once again access the Nigerian market under its Frontier Market classification. J.P. Morgan’s inclusion shows that Nigerian government securities are becoming relevant again to global benchmark investors.

The rating upgrades show that sovereign risk is being reassessed.

The stronger reserves and rising remittances show that the external position has improved.

And the return of international functionality to naira cards provides perhaps the simplest everyday illustration of all.

Three years ago, the reform debate was largely about whether Nigeria could endure the pain.

Today, the question is increasingly about how Nigeria converts the resulting stability into investment, production, jobs and prosperity. What is clear is that the reforms are beginning to yield the international recognition and investor confidence the government sought.

World.title: Gayton slammed over ‘tone-deaf’ tweet amid GBV crisis
World.content:
Minister Gayton McKenzie has been criticised over his comments amid a GBV crisis. Images via X

Gayton McKenzie has been criticised over a “tone deaf” tweet in which he commended himself for bringing Chris Brown – who has a long history of sexual and physical violence allegations against women – to South Africa in 2024. This comes amid heightened gender-based violence concerns, particularly related to the murders of eight women near the Kempton Park area.

The Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture also engaged with a fiery back-and-forth with media personality Bonang Matheba on his X account.

GAYTON MCKENZIE LABELLED ‘TONE-DEAF’ OVER CHRIS BROWN TWEET

On Tuesday, 15 September, Gayton McKenzie trended on X over his back-and-forth tweets with media personality Bonang Matheba, who called the minister out over a lack of funding for South African artists.



Gaytona argued that through his cabinet, he had made a significant impact.

He tweeted: “The Chris Brown concert created the biggest job opportunities for young people in SA who were considered to be unemployable. It was the first time some received a salary. My job as Minister is always to make things easy for our promoters to bring big-name artists to SA”.

The Minister’s mention of the US artist, who has not only been convicted of felony assault in a domestic-violence case, but also linked to multiple other domestic and physical assault charges, sparked backlash online. 

In the comments section, Gayton was inundated with complaints about his “tone-deaf” post.

Here’s what a few had to say…

@Maa_Mshengu: “Are you aware we are currently dealing with a GBV crisis at the moment? Read the room!”



@FaithPale: “You can’t be applauding an abuser, during a GBV crisis. Ooh, wow!”

@blackonees7: “Using Chris Brown at this stage where our beloved country cries over 8 women who had been brutally murdered is such a shame!. All your motivational talks and swindling won’t get you out of this one! Pathetic”

@Ol_etilwe: “Boasting about bringing a GBV perpetrator, mind you”.



I hate Gayton McKenzie, yerrr, he is so tone deaf. pic.twitter.com/3af4asDytI — MaBarçaUnited44⁷🇿🇦 (@ParkJimins_toof) September 15, 2026

‘LET’S HAVE FUN’

Chris Brown performed in South Africa in December 2024, just days after the 16 Days of Activism campaign ended. This came after the broadcast of an Investigation Discovery documentary titled Chris Brown: A History of Violence.

At the time, anti-GBV activists like Women For Change called on the Department of Home Affairs to revoke his visa ahead of the show. Chris seemingly taunted the bid with a jab at the organisation.



Despite the sensitive and serious nature, Minister Gayton McKenzie encouraged South Africans to support the controversial singer.

Addressing the public during his 100-day in-office update, Gayton claimed that he would prioritise hosting major music festivals in the country to attract high-profile artists.

The minister then nonchalantly mentioned Chris Brown, who had been trending at the time over a petition to cancel his shows.



Gayton said: “South Africans love dancing. Chris Brown’s concert was sold out in two hours. Our people are hungry for international acts”.

He added, “Don’t go any further, go to the Chris Brown concert.”

World.title: Cameron Waldeck-Cooks memorial service goes ahead
World.content:
Cameron Waldeck-Cooks's memorial service has taken place. Image via X/Canva

More than a month after her tragic death, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks has been fondly remembered in a memorial service. The St Stithians College student was found dead alongside her partner, Ethan Coetzee – an alumnus – at a game reserve in Mpumalanga.

Police have confirmed that a murder-suicide investigation is open.

Cameron allegedly died from strangulation/suffocation, while it has been reported that Ethan took his own life.



CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS MEMORIAL SERVICE

Over the weekend, the memorial service for Cameron Waldecks-Cooks took place.

The event was private, with no public details on its venue or guest list.

The Facebook and Instagram accounts of the St Stithians water polo team revealed that it had dedicated a game during a tournament over the weekend to Cameron, who also played the sport.



It shared: “This past Sunday, September 13, coincided with the memorial service for our beloved Saints Girls College Gr 11 student, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks. Unable to attend the service while competing on the final day of the St Alban’s Beach Polo tournament, our boys made sure Cameron was with them in spirit. Standing united by the pool, the team wore black armbands with ‘CAM’ written on their arms to honour her.

“Their heartfelt message to Cameron and her loved ones: ‘We wish we could have been there today. You will always be in our thoughts’”.

It’s unclear if the memorial service for Ethan Coetzee has taken place.



WHAT HAPPENED TO ETHAN COETZEE, CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS

In early August, news broke of an alleged murder-suicide involving two St Stithians learners: Grade 11 student Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and 2025 matriculant Ethan Coetzee.

Cameron, 17, and Ethan, 19, were found dead at a lodge in Mpumalanga on Monday, 3 August. Police initially investigated the deaths as an inquest and suspected that no foul play was involved.

However, preliminary findings as well as the opinion of an independent forensic pathologist have stated that Cameron died from strangulation/suffocation.



Ethan’s death is believed to be a suicide. A later report suggested that Ethan was a “jealous” and “controlling” partner to Cameron.

Police subsequently opened a murder case in connection with Cameron’s death. The investigation continues.

In a statement to TimesLive last month, St Stithians stated that it was “aware of difficult conversations this tragedy has prompted”



The Johannesburg private school, which dedicated a Women’s Day message to Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, had come under fire for its tribute to Ethan Coetzee just days earlier.

Many have accused the school of portraying Ethan as a “hero”.

The school declined to respond to rampant rumours about the alleged murder-suicide, including allegations of GBV and possibly drug use.



It shared: “We remain focused on supporting those most affected and caring for our community as it continues to navigate this profound loss”.

St Stithians also vowed to support students and staff affected by the double tragedy.

World.title: Ekurhuleni murders: Here are the eight cases police are investigating
World.content:
SAPS investigators work on the widening Ekurhuleni murder probe, which now includes eight women’s deaths across Kempton Park, Olifantsfontein and KwaThema. Image: SABC

Acting National Police Commissioner Lt-Gen Puleng Dimpane has detailed the eight women’s murder cases now under investigation across Ekurhuleni, as the South African Police Service widens its probe into the killings.

Police are examining five cases in Kempton Park, two in Olifantsfontein and one in KwaThema.

The cases span July to September, with investigators also reviewing earlier dockets to make sure no potentially linked deaths were missed.



SAPS has not confirmed that all eight murders are connected or that one perpetrator is responsible.

1. Kempton Park – 15 July

Police recorded the first case on 15 July.

A 37-year-old woman was found near the R21. Police arrested a suspect two days later and have positively linked him to that murder.



SAPS has not linked the suspect to the other cases.

2. Kempton Park – August

Dimpane said police recorded the second case in Kempton Park during August.

Investigators have included the case in the wider review as they compare evidence, locations and victim profiles.



3. Kempton Park – August

A third Kempton Park case followed during August, according to Dimpane’s breakdown on Tuesday night.

Police are examining that case alongside the others for possible similarities.

4. Kempton Park – September

The fourth case occurred in Kempton Park during September.



The growing cluster of deaths eventually prompted SAPS to bring together detectives, forensic specialists, crime intelligence and other specialised units.

5. Kempton Park – September

Police recorded another Kempton Park case in September, taking the number under investigation in the area to five.

Among the women identified during the broader investigation is Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, 38, who disappeared after leaving her Rhodesfield home for a run.



Her family later formally identified her body at the Germiston mortuary.

6. Olifantsfontein – 14 September

Police found another woman dead in Olifantsfontein on Monday, 14 September.

The discovery widened the investigation beyond the Kempton Park cases and triggered further deployments across Ekurhuleni.



7. KwaThema – 15 September

Officers found another woman dead in KwaThema, Springs, on Tuesday morning, 15 September.

Her decomposed body was discovered on the side of the road.

KwaThema lies about 45km from Kempton Park, where the investigation initially centred. Police have been examining whether there are any forensic or investigative links between the cases.



8. Olifantsfontein – 7 September

Dimpane said police later added another Olifantsfontein case dating back to 7 September after reviewing cases that may be relevant to the investigation.

She acknowledged that police may have missed the case when initially compiling the running total.

The woman was found floating in a river near the Mall of Thembisa area.



Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Maj-Gen Fred Kekana earlier said police had found no visible injuries on the woman but would not exclude the death until investigators completed further work. Public reporting has placed the river discovery in Clayville, near the Mall of Thembisa.

One suspect arrested, another sought

Dimpane also confirmed that police have one suspect in custody and are pursuing another person as investigators follow leads.

The arrested suspect relates to the first Kempton Park murder from July.



Police have not said the suspect is responsible for the other women’s deaths.

SAPS continues to examine whether investigators are dealing with one perpetrator, multiple perpetrators or separate crimes.

R400 000 reward on offer

Police have now offered a R400 000 reward for information that could help investigators make a breakthrough.



“There is R400 000 that we are putting on the table so that we are able to strengthen our investigations,” Dimpane said during Tuesday night’s high-level briefing.

EKURHULENI KILLINGS | Acting National Police Commissioner Lt-Gen Puleng Dimpane says a suspect has been arrested in connection with one of the murders committed in July, while police are pursuing another person of interest. A R400,000 reward has been offered for information that… pic.twitter.com/SQiqlNWHI6 — SABC News (@SABCNews) September 15, 2026

She also appealed to families with missing loved ones to contact police as forensic teams work with pathologists to identify women who remain unknown.



Lesufi: ‘We can’t normalise madness’

Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi has called for urgent action as concern grows across the province.

“We can’t normalise madness; this is madness,” Lesufi said after visiting the Kempton Park area earlier in the investigation.

He also urged residents to report anything they may have seen around the discovery sites, stressing that information that appears insignificant could prove crucial to investigators.



Lesufi said women could not continue living in fear of going about their daily lives and pledged provincial resources to support efforts to improve safety.

Police intensify Ekurhuleni operation

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia confirmed on Tuesday night that the investigation now involves the murders of eight women.

SAPS has established a high-level multidisciplinary team and plans to significantly increase police visibility in Kempton Park and surrounding areas.



President Cyril Ramaphosa has also directed law-enforcement agencies to prioritise the investigation and ordered police to leave “no stone unturned” in bringing those responsible to justice.

For now, investigators continue to treat the evidence as decisive: eight murders are under scrutiny, but police have not yet proved that all eight form part of one pattern.

World.title: Police offer R400 000 reward in Ekurhuleni murder probe
World.content:
SAPS has offered a R400 000 reward for information that could help investigators make a breakthrough in the Ekurhuleni murders probe. Image: Pexels

Acting National Police Commissioner Lt-Gen Puleng Dimpane says police have arrested one suspect and are hunting another as investigators probe the murders of eight women across Ekurhuleni.

Dimpane made the announcement during a high-level briefing on Tuesday night, where police also confirmed a R400 000 reward for information that could help investigators make a breakthrough.

She said police had intensified the investigation, with specialised teams following leads, analysing evidence and working to establish possible links between the cases.



The South African Police Service has not confirmed that the arrested suspect is connected to all eight murders.

Families of missing women urged to come forward

Families who have missing relatives have been urged to contact police as investigators work to identify six of the women.

Police forensic teams are working alongside Gauteng Health pathologists as the identification process continues.

The appeal comes as SAPS examines a rapidly expanding number of cases across Ekurhuleni.

Police have not confirmed that one person or group killed all eight women.

Investigators are comparing forensic evidence, locations, victim profiles and the circumstances surrounding each death to establish whether any of the cases are connected.



Dimpane said police were following specific leads and working to consolidate information from the cases.

SAPS has deployed a high-level multidisciplinary team to drive the investigation.

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia vowed that police would leave “no stone unturned” in bringing those responsible to justice.

Clayville river case added to investigation

Dimpane also confirmed that police are examining the death of a woman found in a river near the Mall of Thembisa in Clayville.

Police found the woman in the water and opened an inquest.

Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Major-General Fred Kekana said earlier that investigators found no visible injuries on her body but included the case in the wider probe to ensure they did not overlook a possible connection.

The woman remains unidentified.

Eight women now form part of wider probe

The investigation initially centred on women found dead in and around Kempton Park before police widened their focus to other parts of Ekurhuleni.

Cachalia confirmed on Tuesday night that authorities were now investigating the murders of eight women.

Police have not released full details about the eighth woman or established that all eight deaths are linked.

SAPS has also announced plans to significantly increase police visibility in Kempton Park and surrounding areas as detectives pursue leads.

World.title: RG Snyman and wife welcome baby girl – See photos + her name!
World.content:
Springbok RG Snyman and his wife, Saskia, have welcomed their first child, a baby girl.

The rugby player, who is based in Ireland, has been out of action in recent months due to an ACL injury sustained in March.

RG SNYMAN IS A DAD!

On her Instagram account, RG Snyman’s wife, Saskia, shared news that the couple had welcomed their first child – a daughter.



The Snymans shared pictures of their newborn as well as her name.

Saskia shared: “Rooks Rose 🤍She’s here, and she’s perfect”.
